## Abstract

The measurement problem of quantum mechanics — the apparent incompatibility between unitary Schrödinger evolution (U) and the stochastic, irreversible reduction (R) invoked at measurement — has stood as the central foundational problem of quantum theory for ninety years. Standard interpretive programmes (Copenhagen, Many-Worlds, Bohmian mechanics, GRW spontaneous localization, decoherence-plus-environmental-selection, Relational Quantum Mechanics, QBism) each address the problem by adding postulates, hidden variables, dynamical modifications, or relational structures to the standard formalism. Each of these programmes, *without exception*, takes the Born rule P = |ψ|² as a postulate or as an assumption requiring independent justification (e.g. Gleason's theorem, decision-theoretic arguments, envariance, frequentist limits). None derives the Born rule from a single underlying physical principle.

The structural advantage of the McGucken framework over every prior interpretive programme can be summarized in the master comparison table below, which subsumes every comparison developed across the present paper — foundational primitives, mathematical structure, the wave function (§V.1), measurement and collapse (§V), the canonical thought experiments (§V.6), information and dynamics (§X), categorical structure (§XIII.10, §XIII.13), and foundational achievement. The table is reproduced in §XVI.5 (Conclusion) as the consolidated summary of all comparisons established formally throughout the paper.

The master table makes the structural advantage immediate. Where every prior programme has multiple foundational postulates and at least one open foundational problem — and where every prior programme either postulates the wave function or interprets a postulated object — the McGucken framework derives every entry in the postulate column as a theorem from a single primitive physical-geometric law $dx_4/dt = ic$. This is not a stylistic difference of presentation; it is a categorical difference of structure, established formally by the space-operator co-generation theorem (Theorem XIII.I), quantified by the two-orders-of-magnitude reduction in K-complexity, and made concrete by the wave function being a derived geometric object (§V.1) rather than an interpretively-flexible postulate. The detailed entries summarized in this master table are established as theorems throughout the paper, with section references in the table cells.

The McGucken framework is unique in deriving the Born rule as a geometric theorem of one foundational principle: the McGucken Principle that the fourth dimension is expanding in a spherically symmetric manner at the velocity of light, dx₄/dt = ic. The depth this derivation gives the McGucken framework into the measurement problem follows directly from what it means to derive Born from a foundational principle rather than postulate it. When Born is postulated, it is a *separate fact* glued onto the linear unitary dynamics — the dynamics evolve states by (U), and the Born rule independently selects probabilities at measurement; the two are logically disconnected, and the measurement problem is precisely the puzzle of how these two disconnected pieces are supposed to fit together at the moment of observation. Every prior interpretive programme inherits this disconnect: Copenhagen patches it with a separate (R) law, Many-Worlds with a branching primitive, Bohmian with quantum equilibrium and a guidance equation, GRW with stochastic localization, decoherence with a system-environment Hamiltonian, RQM with relational facts, and QBism with personal probability assignments. Each of these is, structurally, an *additional ingredient* introduced precisely because (U) and Born are independent inputs whose connection at measurement is not supplied by either of them.

When the McGucken framework derives Born from $dx_4/dt = ic$ as a geometric theorem, the disconnect is dissolved at the source. The Born rule is not added on top of the dynamics — it is a structural feature of the same geometric expansion that produces the dynamics. The squared amplitude $|\psi|^2$ is the SO(3) Haar measure on the McGucken-Sphere wavefront cross-section, the wavefront is the propagation of $x_4$'s spherical advance, and the unitary evolution is the action of $D_M$ on configurations of that wavefront. *Born and (U) are two readings of the same geometric fact*. There is no separate measurement event that has to bridge them, because there is no gap between them. The apparent collapse $R$ is then forced to be what Proposition V.1 establishes — the 3D spatial cross-section reading of an $x_4$-extended state — because there is no other structural slot in the framework where it could live. The preferred basis (Proposition VII.1), the irreversibility (Proposition VI.1), the absence of a separate $(R)$ law (Proposition IX.1), the unitarity itself (Proposition X.2), and the nonlocality without violation of relativistic causality (Proposition VIII.1) all follow as consequences of the same single derivation, because they all descend from the same source.

This is the deeper insight: every component of the standard "measurement problem" — the Born rule, the apparent collapse, the preferred basis, the irreversibility, the nonlocality, the absence of a clean quantum-classical cut — becomes a structural consequence of one geometric principle, and so the standard problem of how these components are supposed to be coordinated at the moment of measurement *does not arise*. The space-operator co-generation theorem (Theorem XIII.I) makes this categorical: because $\mathcal{M}_G$ (the space) and $D_M$ (the operator) are co-generated by $dx_4/dt = ic$, system, apparatus, observer, and dynamics are not four independent categories whose interaction must be coordinated by an additional measurement law — they are projections of one source-pair onto different spatial slices, and the measurement event is the geometric self-intersection $D_M(\Sigma_M(p)) \cap \Sigma_t$ of the source-pair with itself. Proposition XIII.6 establishes that the standard measurement problem cannot even be formulated within the McGucken framework's category structure, because the categorical separation it requires has been dissolved at the source by the co-generation. Born being a theorem rather than a postulate is the doorway to all of this; what follows in this paper is the formal development of what waits behind that doorway.

 This paper establishes the framework's resolution of the measurement problem through seven formal Propositions. **Proposition III.1** derives the Born rule P = |ψ|² as a forced geometric consequence of the squared-amplitude structure of McGucken-wavefront cross-sections, with the three-piece breakdown imported from [MG-Bohmian, §VII] and [MG-QM, Theorem 11]: the complex character of ψ from i as perpendicularity marker of x₄, the quadratic exponent forced by elimination of |ψ|¹, |ψ|³, Re(ψ), Im(ψ) alone as candidates, and the SO(3) Haar-measure shape forced by spherical symmetry. **Proposition IV.1** establishes that the superposition principle (SP) is itself a Grade-2 theorem of dx₄/dt = ic, with linear addition of complex amplitudes the unique geometric overlap operation (among the candidates considered) respecting SO(3) Haar-measure, Lorentz-covariance, linearity, and Born-rule compatibility — a derived structural feature of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront geometry rather than a Hilbert-space postulate. **Proposition V.1** establishes that the apparent collapse R is not a separate dynamical law but the 3D spatial cross-section reading of an x₄-extended state, with no separate (R) postulate required. §V.6 applies this resolution directly to the two canonical thought experiments — Schrödinger's cat (1935) and Wigner's friend (1961) — showing that Schrödinger's reductio is *vindicated* (the cat is in a definite state because its Compton frequency is enormous and decoherence is below any detection threshold) and Wigner's apparent paradox is *dissolved* (the friend's definite outcome and Wigner's superposition description are projections of one $x_4$-extended state onto different spatial slices, with consistency guaranteed by $x_4$-coincidence). Section V.bis extends the structural derivation strategy from the wave function to fields more broadly — establishing that classical fields (electromagnetic, gravitational), the wave function as a complex scalar field, quantum fields in QFT, and gauge fields are all derived structures rather than independent postulates. Every field type descends from the source-tuple $F_M = (\Sigma_M, \mathcal{G}_M, \mathcal{M}_G, D_M, \mathcal{S}_M, \mathcal{A}_M)$ as a theorem: classical fields are curvatures or potentials of McGucken-derived bundles; the wave function is the cross-section reading of an $x_4$-extended complex scalar field on $\mathcal{M}_G$; quantum fields in QFT are $D_M$-flow structures on Fock space; gauge fields are connections on principal bundles whose Lie-group structure descends from the McGucken Symmetry's internal action (settled for U(1); programmatically in place for SU(2)$_L$ via Cl(1,3)$^+$ spinor structure; open research for SU(3)$_c$ via the substrate-scale Connes-descent route of [MG-Connes, Theorem H]). The McGucken framework's commitment is uniform: every aspect of every field type is ultimately a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$, and the apparent diversity of field types in standard physics is a structural feature of which sector of the McGucken Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}_{\rm McG} = \mathcal{L}_{\rm kin} + \mathcal{L}_{\rm Dirac} + \mathcal{L}_{\rm YM} + \mathcal{L}_{\rm EH}$ governs the flow. **Proposition VI.1** establishes that the irreversibility of measurement is the same x₄-monotonicity that grounds the second law of thermodynamics throughout the McGucken corpus [MG-Entropy, MG-Horizon], requiring no separate stochastic dynamics. **Proposition VII.1** establishes that the preferred basis is selected by environmental Compton-frequency decoherence, with the cut between quantum and classical specified by a concrete physical mechanism rather than left arbitrary. **Proposition VIII.1** establishes that quantum nonlocality is the geometric consequence of x₄-mediated correlation through the six-sense null-surface identity of the McGucken Sphere, with the First Law of Nonlocality (all nonlocality begins in locality) supplying the structural account [MG-Nonloc]. **Proposition VIII.2** establishes that the no-signaling theorem of quantum mechanics is a property of the physical apparatus itself rather than of the algebraic formalism: probability cloaks nonlocality, with the same SO(3) symmetry of x₄'s expansion producing both the Tsirelson-saturating correlations and the marginal flatness, and Corollaries VIII.2.1–VIII.2.2 establishing that no-signaling is exact (not approximate) and that nonlocality and irreducible probability are two faces of the single expansion dx₄/dt = ic — dissolving Shimony's "peaceful coexistence" puzzle. **Proposition IX.1** establishes that the absence of a separate (R) law is itself a theorem rather than an interpretive choice, with the apparent (R) phenomenon reduced to the 3D-projection reading of unitary x₄-evolution.

§X extends the framework's resolution from the measurement problem to the black hole information paradox, showing that both are the same problem at different scales. Through Propositions X.1 (information preservation as a theorem of x₄'s smoothness), X.2 (unitarity is derived rather than postulated), X.3 (the Page curve as a theorem of x₄-coincidence redistribution during evaporation), X.4 (the structural identification of the measurement problem and the information paradox), and X.5 (the McGucken framework as, among the surveyed frameworks, the one that derives unitarity itself rather than postulating it), the section establishes that information is never destroyed in any physical process — the preservation is a Grade-2 theorem of x₄'s smoothness and norm-preservation rather than an additional postulate, and the same x₄-coincidence mechanism that resolves the measurement problem (Proposition V.1) resolves the information paradox at the cosmological scale.

§XI develops the structural punchline: where the original presentation already established the Born rule as a theorem, the analysis establishes that the *foundational pair* (Q1) linearity and (Q3) Born — the structural core of quantum mechanics — is *jointly* derived from one underlying principle. The Hilbert-space postulate (Q1) is no longer foundational; the Born rule (Q3) is no longer foundational; the apparent collapse (R) is no longer a separate dynamical law; unitarity itself is no longer a foundational commitment. All four are derived consequences of dx₄/dt = ic. The McGucken framework is the only known quantum framework with this joint-derivation property; all seven prior interpretive programmes and all four major information-paradox resolutions either take these structures as postulates or derive them from auxiliary frameworks while leaving deeper structures foundational.

## I. Introduction: The Ninety-Year Problem

### I.1 Two dynamical laws

Standard quantum mechanics, as developed by Heisenberg, Schrödinger, Dirac, Born, and von Neumann between 1925 and 1932 and consolidated in the Dirac–von Neumann axiomatic system [Dirac1958; vonNeumann1932], operates with two distinct dynamical laws:

**(U) Unitary evolution.** Between measurements, the state vector |ψ⟩ evolves according to the Schrödinger equation iℏ ∂|ψ⟩/∂t = Ĥ|ψ⟩. The evolution is deterministic, linear, and time-reversible. It preserves superposition: if |ψ⟩ = α|a⟩ + β|b⟩ at time t = 0, then at time t > 0 the state is |ψ(t)⟩ = α|a(t)⟩ + β|b(t)⟩, with |a(t)⟩ and |b(t)⟩ the unitarily evolved components.

**(R) Reduction at measurement.** Upon measurement of an observable Â with eigenstates {|a\_i⟩}, the state vector "collapses" to one of the eigenstates: |ψ⟩ → |a\_i⟩, with probability P(a\_i) = |⟨a\_i|ψ⟩|² (the Born rule). The reduction is stochastic, nonlinear, and time-irreversible. It destroys superposition: after the measurement, only one component survives.

### I.2 The problem

(U) and (R) are logically incompatible as fundamental dynamical laws. Five sharp difficulties:

**(i) When does (R) apply?** No principled rule specifies when (R) replaces (U). A measurement apparatus is itself a quantum system, so its interaction with the measured system should be governed by (U), producing a superposition of apparatus pointer states — never a single definite outcome. The standard pedagogical solution invokes a "quantum-classical cut" placed somewhere between the microscopic system and the macroscopic apparatus, but the placement is arbitrary [Bell1990, *Against Measurement*].

**(ii) Why (R) at all?** If (U) is the true dynamics, (R) is unnecessary — measurement should produce a superposition of "pointer reading + outcome" branches, with all branches present. If (R) is the true dynamics, it must be triggered by something. Standard quantum mechanics names neither trigger nor mechanism.

**(iii) Why P = |ψ|²?** The Born rule is a postulate. The squared-amplitude form is taken as given; no derivation from a deeper principle is offered in the standard formalism. Multiple later attempts — Gleason's theorem [Gleason1957], decision-theoretic derivations [Deutsch1999; Wallace2012], envariance [Zurek2005], frequentist limit theorems [Hartle1968] — each derive |ψ|² from auxiliary assumptions that themselves require justification.

**(iv) Why irreversibility?** (U) is time-reversible; (R) is not. Where does the asymmetry come from? Standard quantum mechanics gives no answer; environmental decoherence accounts (Zurek, Joos, Zeh) supply *part* of an answer (irreversibility from environmental information leakage) but require additional input on the preferred basis and the Born rule.

**(v) Why nonlocality?** Bell's theorem [Bell1964] establishes that quantum correlations cannot be explained by local hidden variables. The CHSH inequality [CHSH1969] is empirically violated up to the Tsirelson bound 2√2 [Tsirelson1980]. The standard formalism reports the violation and proves the no-signalling theorem, but supplies no geometric account of how distant entangled particles maintain correlations consistent with relativistic causality.

### I.3 The seven interpretive programmes

Over ninety years, seven major interpretive programmes have addressed the measurement problem. Each adds structure to the standard formalism; none subtracts; and *none* derives the Born rule from a single foundational principle.

**Copenhagen** (Bohr, Heisenberg, 1927–1932): the wavefunction represents the experimenter's knowledge; (R) is the update of knowledge upon measurement; the quantum-classical cut is operational, placed wherever the experimenter draws it. The framework declines to give an ontological account of (R) and treats the Born rule as a postulate.

**Many-Worlds (Everett, 1957; DeWitt, Wallace, 2012):** all branches of the (U)-evolved superposition are equally real; (R) is the apparent restriction to one branch from the standpoint of an observer within a branch. The Born rule is not a postulate of the dynamics but is recovered through decision-theoretic or envariance arguments [Deutsch1999; Wallace2012; Zurek2005], each requiring auxiliary assumptions.

**Bohmian mechanics (de Broglie, 1927; Bohm, 1952; Dürr–Goldstein–Zanghì, 1992):** the wavefunction guides hidden variables (definite particle positions) via the guidance equation; (R) is apparent only and arises from observer ignorance of the hidden variables. The Born rule is derived from the equilibrium hypothesis (particles distributed according to |ψ|² initially), but the equilibrium hypothesis itself is an additional postulate [Valentini, 1991 — quantum non-equilibrium would predict deviations from |ψ|²].

**GRW (Ghirardi–Rimini–Weber, 1986):** the Schrödinger equation is modified to include stochastic spontaneous-localization terms; (R) is a real physical process governed by these terms, with parameters λ (rate) and a (localization width) chosen to match observed quantum behavior at small scales and classical behavior at large scales. The Born rule emerges from the localization dynamics, but the dynamics itself is added by hand and the parameters are phenomenological.

**Decoherence-plus-environmental-selection (Zurek, Joos, Zeh, 1981–2003):** environmental coupling rapidly diagonalizes the system's reduced density matrix in a specific (pointer) basis, suppressing macroscopic interference and producing apparent (R) without any modification of (U). The framework correctly explains why macroscopic superpositions become unobservable but does not derive the Born rule and does not by itself solve the preferred-basis problem (which basis is the pointer basis depends on the system-environment coupling, and identifying that coupling requires additional input).

**Relational Quantum Mechanics (Rovelli, 1996):** the wavefunction is relational — it describes the state of one system relative to another observer-system. (R) is the update of one system's information about another. The framework takes the Born rule as a postulate and does not derive it.

**QBism (Fuchs, Mermin, Schack, 2002–present):** the wavefunction represents the personal beliefs of a single agent; (R) is the agent's Bayesian update upon experiencing a measurement outcome. The Born rule is taken as a normative constraint on the agent's beliefs, justified by Dutch-book arguments. The framework explicitly declines to derive the Born rule from a deeper physical principle, treating it as a primitive coherence requirement on the agent.

### I.4 What is missing

Every one of the seven programmes either takes the Born rule as a postulate or derives it from auxiliary assumptions that themselves require independent justification. None traces P = |ψ|² to a single foundational principle. Each programme also addresses (R) by adding structure — branches, hidden variables, stochastic localizations, environmental couplings, relational frames, or epistemic constraints. None reduces the apparent (R) phenomenon to a *theorem* of (U) plus a single geometric principle.

What is missing is a single foundational source from which:

* The Born rule P = |ψ|² is *derived*, not postulated.
* The apparent (R) phenomenon is reduced to a *theorem* of (U) plus the foundational source.
* Quantum nonlocality is given a *geometric* mechanism consistent with relativistic causality.
* The preferred basis is selected by a *concrete physical mechanism* with no operational arbitrariness.
* The whole structure follows from *one* principle, not a combination of postulates.

This paper establishes that the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic is exactly such a foundational source, and that the measurement problem is, in the McGucken framework, a chain of formal theorems descending from this single geometric principle.

### I.4.1 The primacy of dx₄/dt = ic over its integrated form x₄ = ict

A point of structural emphasis applies throughout the paper. The McGucken framework rests on the *physical-geometric* primitive

  dx₄/dt = ic,

the assertion that the fourth dimension x₄ is, at every spacetime event, expanding in a spherically symmetric manner at the velocity of light, with i the perpendicularity marker recording the orientation of x₄ relative to the spatial three. The integrated form x₄ = ict is the algebraic consequence of this differential primitive (with C = 0 fixed by source-origin convention) — a kinematic identity, not an independent postulate.

Wherever the paper writes "x₄ = ict" — in the perpendicularity marker for the wavefunction (Proposition III.1, Piece 1), in the constraint Φ\_M (Theorem XIII.A), in the Wick rotation identity (Theorem XIII.E), in the Lorentzian wave operator projection (Theorem XIII.F), or anywhere else — the algebraic form is to be understood as encoding the underlying physical-geometric fact: that x₄ expands at the velocity of light, spherically symmetrically, from every spacetime event. Treating "x₄ = ict" as mere mathematical bookkeeping (as in some standard accounts of Wick rotation or complex-time formalism) loses the physical content that the McGucken Principle restores. The framework's derivational chain — Born rule, Schrödinger equation, Hilbert space, path integral, unitarity, the Page curve — descends from the *physical fact of spherical expansion at c*, with the algebraic form x₄ = ict being only the integral expression of that fact.

This primacy of the differential physical primitive over its integrated algebraic form is the structural feature that distinguishes the McGucken framework from prior frameworks employing complex-time formalism (Wick rotation, Schwinger's proper-time representation, Euclidean path integrals). Each of those frameworks employs the algebraic form x₄ = ict (or its functional equivalent) as a calculational device, with the imaginary unit serving as a Wick-rotation parameter or analytic-continuation prescription. None of them treats the differential primitive dx₄/dt = ic as a *physical* statement about the geometry of spacetime — none of them asserts that x₄ is, in physical fact, expanding at c from every event. The McGucken framework is the first to make this physical-geometric identification; the formal consequences developed in the present paper follow from the physical content of the primitive, not from the algebraic shorthand in which it is sometimes encoded.

### I.4.1-bis The geometry is forced: from dx₄/dt = ic to the expanding sphere, hidden in plain sight in x₄ = ict

The differential reading of §I.4.1 makes dx₄/dt = ic a physical expansion. The next step is a consequence forced by that expansion, requiring no further posit: its spatial profile is compelled to be spherically symmetric, and the object so compelled — the expanding sphere — is the generative source of the metric, the arrow of time, and nonlocality alike. The recognition proceeds in layered steps, each forced by the one above.

*Step 1 (the coordinate is given).* $x_4 = ict$ is the imaginary fourth coordinate of Poincaré (1906) and Minkowski (1908). As written it is static — a coordinate label with no dynamical content, the frozen block Eddington described as carrying "no signboard to indicate that it is a one-way street."

*Step 2 (the derivative is physical).* Differentiating with respect to $t$ yields $dx_4/dt = ic$: the statement that $x_4$ physically advances at rate $c$. This is the change of content of §I.4.1 — a static coordinate identity becomes an active rate, and an active rate is a physical claim that something moves.

*Step 3 (the geometry is forced).* Ask how $x_4$ advances relative to the three spatial dimensions — in what spatial profile. The advance cannot select any particular spatial direction or subset of directions, because nothing in "$x_4$ expands relative to $x_1x_2x_3$" privileges one spatial direction over another: $x_4$ is perpendicular to all three spatial axes equally, which is exactly what the marker $i$ records, and a perpendicularity that is symmetric across $x_1, x_2, x_3$ supplies no basis on which to prefer $\hat x$ over $\hat y$ over $\hat z$. An expansion with no preferred spatial direction is isotropic; the unique isotropic spatial profile is the sphere. Therefore, *given that nothing in dx₄/dt = ic couples to a preferred spatial direction* (which the symmetric perpendicularity of $x_4$ to the spatial three guarantees), the expansion is spherically symmetric of necessity, and $dx_4/dt = ic$ is the expansion of a sphere — the McGucken Sphere (Definition of §II). This is the same form of argument by which the Cosmological Principle derives the isotropy of the Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker metric: no preferred direction forces isotropy, and isotropy forces the spherically symmetric form. The spherical symmetry is compelled by the impossibility of the perpendicular fourth dimension selecting a spatial direction to expand along; it is not a clause adjoined to the Principle.

*Step 4 (the sphere was hidden in plain sight).* The expanding sphere was therefore latent in $x_4 = ict$ from 1908 onward. Poincaré and Minkowski wrote the coordinate; its differentiation into a physical rate forces isotropy; isotropy is a sphere; and so the sphere sat inside the coordinate, unread, for over a century. The framework's recognition is the reading of that latent geometry — seeing, in the coordinate everyone had written, the expanding sphere no one had seen.

*The sphere is generative.* Once the sphere is compelled, the principal structures of physics follow from it as consequences of one forced geometry, each established as a theorem in the body and corpus:

- *Minkowski and Lorentzian spacetime.* Integrating the rate returns $x_4 = ict$, and squaring it, with $(ic)^2 = -c^2$, returns the Lorentzian signature: the metric is the squared rate of the sphere's expansion (Lemma 2.5). The light cone is the locus the expanding wavefront traces. The spacetime that the orthodox tradition takes as its starting arena is the sphere's own shadow.

- *Entropy, the Second Law, and the arrow of time.* The sphere's volume increases as it expands, and the expansion is monotonic — the advance is $+ic$, with no $-ic$ branch in the physical fact. An expanding, dissipating volume that cannot un-expand is the arrow of time and the Second Law: the monotonic increase of the sphere's volume drives time and all its arrows and asymmetries (Proposition VI.1; the strict $+ic$ monotonicity, and [MG-Entropy]). Time's asymmetry is the geometry of an expanding volume, requiring no separate thermodynamic posit.

- *Nonlocality, and thence probability.* The sphere is one $x_4$-coincident object spread across an ever-larger surface (the outbound First Law of Nonlocality): a single event distributed across a region, which is nonlocality by construction. Because the surface is isotropic — forced in Step 3 — a detection that localizes the event draws its outcome from the unique isotropic measure on the sphere, the SO(3)-Haar measure, which is the Born density $|\psi|^2$ (Proposition III.1; §V.5-bis, §VIII). Probability follows from the nonlocality of the isotropic sphere; it is the isotropic measure of the one nonlocal surface, made observable in the statistics of many detections.

The economy is therefore sharper than the fewest-posits criterion usually permits. The Principle is one dynamical fact; its geometry is compelled rather than freely chosen (isotropy, hence the sphere, forced by the perpendicularity of $x_4$ to the spatial three); and the compelled sphere is pregnant with the metric, the arrow of time, and nonlocality-with-probability. One fact, one forced geometry, and from it the range of phenomena the founders sought to cover from the fewest principles.

### I.4.2 Postulate-by-postulate map onto the standard mathematical formulation of quantum mechanics

The mathematical formulation of quantum mechanics, in its canonical statement, is a list of postulates established by Dirac (1930) and von Neumann (1932) — the Dirac–von Neumann axioms [Dirac1930; vonNeumann1932]. The contemporary canonical statement of these postulates, freely available and broadly referenced, is the Wikipedia article *Mathematical formulation of quantum mechanics* [WikiQM2026], which we adopt as the canonical reference statement of the standard formulation throughout this paper. The Wikipedia article enumerates approximately ten foundational postulates — Hilbert space (Postulate I), composite systems (tensor product), observables as Hermitian operators (Postulate II.a), the Born rule (Postulate II.b), the collapse rule (Postulate II.c), the Schrödinger equation (Postulate III), Stone's theorem on time evolution, spin, the symmetrization principle (Pauli), and the POVM generalization. Each postulate is *asserted* as a foundational structural feature of the theory; none is derived from a deeper physical principle.

The structural advantage of the McGucken framework over the standard Dirac–von Neumann formulation is that *every postulate listed in the canonical Wikipedia statement of the standard formulation is recovered as a derived theorem* of the present paper, with the single underlying physical primitive being dx₄/dt = ic — the assertion that the fourth dimension x₄ is, at every spacetime event, expanding in a spherically symmetric manner at the velocity of light. The formal cross-walk is the following:

What changes is the foundational layer: instead of the ten or so independent postulates of the Dirac–von Neumann formulation, there is one physical-geometric primitive, dx₄/dt = ic, from which the postulates descend as theorems. The Kolmogorov-complexity bit-budget of the foundational layer drops from approximately 10⁴ bits (the standard postulate set) to approximately 10² bits (the single physical primitive), while every formal consequence the standard formulation produces is preserved.

This is the rigorous physical content behind the philosophy: the McGucken framework is rooted in *physics*, not in interpretation. The standard mathematical formulation of QM, as canonically stated on Wikipedia [WikiQM2026], is the *the dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel* algebraic shadow of the *the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel* geometric content carried by dx₄/dt = ic, with the two channels related by the structural duality developed in §XIII (the dual-channel architecture of Theorem XIII.A through Theorem XIII.N). ### I.4.3 Newton's absolute time completed: the Cave allegory and the physical-invariant status of dx₄/dt = ic

In the Scholium to the Definitions of the *Principia* (1687), Newton wrote:

> *"Absolute, true, and mathematical time, of itself, and from its own nature, flows equably without relation to anything external, and by another name is called duration; relative, apparent, and common time, is some sensible and external (whether accurate or unequable) measure of duration by the means of motion, which is commonly used instead of true time; such as an hour, a day, a month, a year."* [Newton1687, Scholium I]

Newton's intuition was profound. He recognized that the time we *measure* on clocks — the time of pendulums and water-flow, of caesium hyperfine transitions and pulsar rotations — is not the foundational time, but a derivative reading of something deeper. The clocks of laboratory practice are "sensible and external" measures; behind them, Newton insisted, stands an *absolute, mathematical* time that "flows equably" of its own physical nature, independent of the apparatus that measures it. Three centuries of physics — special and general relativity, quantum mechanics, statistical mechanics, cosmology — have rejected the *details* of Newton's account (clocks tick at different rates in different gravitational potentials, in different inertial frames, in different thermal environments) while preserving the *intuition* behind it: that there is something physically primary about temporal becoming, something that is not reducible to the readings of any particular clock.

Newton came close to dx₄/dt = ic; he did not arrive at it. What he called *absolute, true, mathematical time* — the something whose uniform flow is independent of any measuring apparatus — is, under the McGucken Principle, the physical-geometric expansion of the fourth dimension at the velocity of light:

  *dx₄/dt = ic,    at every event of spacetime, in every inertial frame, in every gravitational potential.*

The rate of x₄'s expansion is a *physical invariant*. It does not slow in stronger gravitational fields, accelerate in inertial frames, dilate at relativistic velocities, or pause during quantum measurements. Every clock ever built — every pendulum, every cesium fountain, every pulsar, every neutron-star spin — measures a *shadow* of x₄'s expansion projected onto the apparatus's worldline; the rates we measure with clocks are sensible-and-external readings, the rate of x₄ itself is the absolute-and-mathematical flow Newton intuited.

#### I.4.3.1 The Cave allegory

The relation between dx₄/dt = ic and the time we measure on clocks is the relation between Plato's *forms* and Plato's *shadows*. Plato wrote of prisoners in a cave who, seeing only the shadows cast by objects illuminated by a fire behind them, mistake the shadows for reality [Plato\_Republic, Book VII, 514a–520a]. Released from the cave, the prisoner sees the objects themselves and the fire that illuminates them, and recognizes that the cave's shadows were derived forms — projections of a higher reality onto the limited surface of the cave wall.

The structure of the McGucken framework is the structure of Plato's Cave applied to time. The various times of physics — Schrödinger's $t$ in $i\hbar\partial_t\psi = \hat H\psi$, Einstein's proper time $\tau$ along a worldline, the laboratory $t$ on the clock, the cosmological $t$ in the Friedmann equations, the thermodynamic $t$ in $dS/dt = (3/2)k_B/t > 0$ — are shadows on different cave walls of one luminous reality. The fire that casts them is dx₄/dt = ic; the cave walls are the various physical apparatus that read the projections. In each cave, the prisoners of the apparatus see only the shadow on their particular wall: the quantum-mechanics observer sees the Schrödinger $t$ in the equation; the general-relativity observer sees the proper time $\tau$ on the geodesic; the thermodynamics observer sees the strict $dS/dt > 0$ on the apparatus. Each takes the local shadow for the reality.

The McGucken Principle releases the prisoner from the cave. The shadow of QM-time on the cave wall of the Schrödinger equation, the shadow of GR-time on the cave wall of the proper-time interval, the shadow of thermo-time on the cave wall of the Second Law — these are *three different shadows of the same fire*. The fire is the physical-geometric fact that x₄ is, at every spacetime event, expanding in a spherically symmetric manner at the velocity of light. The shadow is the local apparatus-reading. The McGucken framework is the framework that names the fire.

#### I.4.3.2 Mapping the three caves

Three caves in particular have dominated twentieth-century physics, each with its own time-shadow:

**The quantum-mechanics cave.** The shadow on this wall is the time $t$ in the Schrödinger equation $i\hbar\partial_t\psi = \hat H\psi$, the $t$ in the path-integral measure $\mathcal{D}\gamma\,\exp(iS[\gamma]/\hbar)$, the $t$ in the Heisenberg evolution $\hat O(t) = U^\dagger(t)\hat O U(t)$, the $t$ in the canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ generating the unitary group. The standard QM observer takes this $t$ as primitive — the time of the equation — without asking what physical-geometric fact makes the equation take that form. The McGucken Principle answers: the $t$ in $i\hbar\partial_t\psi = \hat H\psi$ is the projection of x₄'s expansion at $ic$ onto the laboratory frame, with the $i$ in $i\hbar$ being the perpendicularity marker of x₄ relative to the spatial three (Theorem XIII.E; Theorem XIII.J), and with the Hamiltonian itself being the generator of x₄-translations by Stone's theorem (Proposition X.2). The QM-time is the laboratory shadow of x₄'s expansion in the QM cave.

**The general-relativity cave.** The shadow on this wall is the proper time $\tau$ along a worldline, the coordinate time $t$ in the Schwarzschild metric, the cosmological time $t$ in the Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker metric, the redshift parameter $z = a(t_0)/a(t_e) - 1$ relating present and emission times. The GR observer takes these times as observer-dependent quantities — proper time depends on the worldline, coordinate time depends on the chart — but takes the geometric structure that produces them (the Lorentzian metric) as primitive. The McGucken Principle answers: the Lorentzian metric and its Schwarzschild and FLRW solutions are projections of x₄'s expansion under the principle; proper time $\tau$ is the relativistic-invariant reading of $x_4/(ic)$ along a worldline, with $d\tau = dx_4/(ic)$ the differential statement, and the cosmological scale factor $a(t)$ governed by Friedmann is the radial-cross-section measure of the cosmological McGucken Sphere [MG-Cosmology]. The GR-times are the geometric shadows of x₄'s expansion in the GR cave.

**The thermodynamics cave.** The shadow on this wall is the strict positivity $dS/dt > 0$ — the Second Law of Thermodynamics, with its specific entropy-increase rate $dS/dt = (3/2)k_B/t$ derived in [MG-Thermodynamics, Theorem 9] from the McGucken-Sphere geometry. The standard thermodynamics observer takes this strict positivity as a statistical tendency emergent from time-symmetric microscopic dynamics, with Boltzmann's 1877 retreat to the statistical interpretation locking in the hierarchy of "time-symmetric Schrödinger equation" above "statistical Second Law." The McGucken Principle answers (Theorem X.C): the Second Law is *not* a derivative statistical tendency. The strict $dS/dt > 0$ is the entropy-increase reading of x₄'s monotonic expansion at $+ic$, with the strict positivity having no $−ic$ counterpart because x₄ cannot contract. The thermo-time is the entropy-increase shadow of x₄'s expansion in the thermodynamics cave.

All three caves project the same fire. The QM $t$ on the laboratory wall, the GR $\tau$ on the worldline wall, the thermo $t$ on the entropy wall — three shadows, one fire. The conservation laws of physics inherit from the same source: x₄'s expansion is the physical-geometric invariant whose symmetry, the McGucken Symmetry [MG-Symmetry], is the *father symmetry* from which all other conservation laws descend. By a Noether-like reasoning, an invariant physical quantity defines a symmetry, the symmetry generates conservation laws; under the McGucken Principle, x₄'s expansion is the primal invariant, the McGucken Symmetry is the primal symmetry, and energy-momentum conservation, charge conservation, baryon-number conservation, lepton-number conservation, CPT invariance — every conservation law of physics — descends from the same source [MG-Lagrangian §IV.4].

#### I.4.3.3 The five arrows of time as five shadows of one fire

Theorem IX.B in §IX.5 establishes that the five empirically-distinct arrows of time identified in the philosophy of physics literature [Penrose1989; Price1996; Albert2000] — the thermodynamic arrow (entropy increase), the cosmological arrow (universal expansion), the radiative arrow (retarded radiation), the quantum-measurement arrow (irreversible measurement outcomes), and the psychological/biological arrow (memory and aging) — are necessarily aligned. Under the Cave allegory, this alignment has its natural reading: the five arrows are *five shadows of one fire*. Each arrow is the time-shadow projected onto a different cave wall — thermodynamic apparatus, cosmological observer, electromagnetic radiator, quantum apparatus, biological organism — but the fire that casts them all is dx₄/dt = ic. The alignment is not an empirical coincidence requiring auxiliary postulates (the Past Hypothesis, statistical-mechanical fine-tuning, anthropic selection); the alignment is the trivial consequence of all five arrows being shadows of one physical-invariant flow.

#### I.4.3.4 What Newton intuited that the twentieth century forgot

The twentieth-century rejection of Newtonian absolute time was, in retrospect, an overcorrection. Einstein's relativity established that there is no preferred frame for the *coordinate* time $t$ of clocks; different inertial observers and different gravitational potentials produce different clock-readings, and there is no privileged $t$ among them. From this, the twentieth-century consensus drew the broader conclusion that *all* notions of absolute time must be abandoned — and with them, the Newtonian intuition that something physically primary stands behind clock-time. The "block universe" of Gödel and Putnam, the timeless universe of Wheeler–DeWitt, the relational time of Rovelli — each in its way reflects the consensus that time is not a fundamental physical structure but a derivative bookkeeping convenience.

The McGucken Principle vindicates Newton's intuition while preserving Einstein's correction. Coordinate time $t$ on a clock is, as Einstein established, not absolute — clocks tick differently in different gravitational potentials, different inertial frames. But the rate of x₄'s expansion — the rate at which the fourth dimension unfolds at every event of spacetime — *is* absolute. dx₄/dt = ic at every event, in every frame, in every gravitational potential. The clocks of laboratory practice are sensible-and-external measures, in Newton's phrase; the *physical-geometric expansion rate of x₄* is the absolute-and-mathematical flow Newton intuited. Newton wrote without knowing about relativity, without knowing about quantum mechanics, without knowing about thermodynamics in its modern form — yet he saw, three centuries before the McGucken Principle, that some physical-geometric fact about temporal becoming had to be primary, and that the times of clocks had to be derivative readings of it. He came close. He named it *absolute, true, mathematical time*. We now name it dx₄/dt = ic.

The same intuition surfaced in the philosophical tradition repeatedly. Einstein himself wrote: *"My solution was really for the very concept of time, that is, that time is not absolutely defined but there is an inseparable connection between time and the signal [light] velocity"* [Einstein1912]. The inseparable connection between time and the signal velocity is, under the McGucken Principle, the differential statement dx₄/dt = ic itself: time is the coordinate along which x₄ expands at velocity $c$. Wheeler wrote: *"Should we be prepared to see some day a new structure for the foundations of physics that does away with time? Yes, because 'time' is in trouble"* [Wheeler1988]. Time as understood in the twentieth century was indeed in trouble — irreducibly conflicted between QM-$t$, GR-$\tau$, and thermo-$t$ readings — but the McGucken framework's resolution is not to *do away with* time but to relocate it to its proper structural level: time-as-coordinate is derivative; the rate of x₄'s expansion is primary.

#### I.4.3.5 The structural payoff

Under the Cave allegory, several long-standing puzzles in the foundations of physics dissolve as forced consequences of *one shadow being mistaken for the fire*:

* **The "problem of time" in canonical quantum gravity** — the apparent timelessness of the Wheeler–DeWitt equation $\hat H |\Psi\rangle = 0$, which has no $\partial_t$ — is dissolved when one recognizes that the Wheeler–DeWitt $t$ was the *QM-cave shadow*, and the underlying x₄-expansion is what remains when one projects out the cave wall. The Wheeler–DeWitt timelessness is the timelessness of the fire, not the timelessness of the universe.

* **The arrow-of-time problem** — the apparent conflict between time-symmetric microscopic dynamics and time-asymmetric thermodynamic macroscopic dynamics — is dissolved when one recognizes that the microscopic dynamics is *not* time-symmetric (Theorem IX.A), and the five arrows are five shadows of the same +ic fire (Theorem IX.B, §I.4.3.3 above).

* **The measurement problem** — the apparent conflict between unitary Schrödinger evolution and irreversible measurement outcomes — is dissolved when one recognizes that both are shadows on different cave walls of dx₄/dt = ic, with the apparent irreversibility being the Euclidean-signature reading and the apparent unitarity being the Lorentzian-signature reading of the same underlying x₄-expansion (Theorem X.B; Corollary X.B.1).

* **The Past Hypothesis** — the apparent need for Penrose's $10^{-10^{123}}$ fine-tuning of the early-universe Weyl curvature to set the low-entropy initial condition — is dissolved when one recognizes that x₄'s origin is geometrically necessarily the lowest-entropy moment, with the McGucken Sphere having zero radius at $t = 0$ [MG-Thermodynamics, Theorem 13]. The low-entropy initial condition is *forced* by the same fire that generates the Schrödinger equation; no auxiliary fine-tuning is required.

* **The "peaceful coexistence" of quantum nonlocality and relativistic causality** — Shimony's puzzle of how QM is genuinely nonlocal yet relativity is preserved — is dissolved when one recognizes that nonlocality and the no-signaling theorem are *two shadows of one geometric object* (Proposition VIII.2; §VIII.4): the wavefront identity carries the nonlocal correlation, the wavefront intensity carries the marginal flatness, and the SO(3) symmetry of x₄'s expansion calibrates the two so they cancel exactly.

In each case, the dissolution is the same dissolution: what appeared as an apparent conflict between two physical phenomena is recognized as the apparent conflict between two shadows of the same fire. The phenomena were not in conflict; the conflict was in the cave-wall reading.

The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic functions here as the fire that casts the shadows — a physical-geometric primitive, not an interpretive overlay on an existing formalism. Newton intuited that the fire must exist — that there must be something physically primary behind clock-time. Einstein corrected the *details* of Newton's account but preserved the intuition. Wheeler warned that time was in trouble and asked for a deeper structure. The McGucken Principle is that structure. The time we measure on our watches and clocks are shadows of the light cast by dx₄/dt = ic in various caves — quantum mechanics, general relativity, thermodynamics, cosmology, biology — and the structural payoff developed throughout the present paper is the recognition, in each cave, that the local shadow is derivative of the same fire that casts the shadows in every other cave.

The McGucken framework is what becomes possible when the prisoner is released from the cave.

### I.4.4 The dual-channel architecture as the structural mechanism of the resolution

The cave allegory of §I.4.3 identifies dx₄/dt = ic as the *fire* and the various time-readings of physics as *shadows* on different cave walls. The shadow-and-fire relation is structurally precise: dx₄/dt = ic admits two *parallel readings* — an algebraic-symmetry reading (*the Algebraic Channel*) and a geometric-propagation reading (*the Geometric Channel*) — and every fundamental structure of physics is the projection of one or both readings onto a specific apparatus context. This subsection consolidates the dual-channel architecture as the structural mechanism behind the resolutions developed throughout the paper, drawing on the full development in [MG-Duality §§II–IX].

**the Algebraic Channel** — the algebraic-symmetry face of dx₄/dt = ic — reads the principle as a statement about *invariance*: the rate ic is unchanged under translations, rotations, and Lorentz boosts that respect the McGucken foliation. The unitary representations of these symmetries are the operator algebra of quantum mechanics — Stone's theorem on time translation [Stone1932], Wigner's classification on the Poincaré group [Wigner1939], Stone–von Neumann on canonical commutation [vonNeumann1931], the Heisenberg picture of operator evolution, the commutator [q̂, p̂] = iℏ. The *i* in dx₄/dt = ic is *interior* to the Algebraic Channel's operators: it is the algebraic record of x₄'s perpendicularity, transmitted through Stone's theorem into the operator algebra.

**the Geometric Channel** — the geometric-propagation face of dx₄/dt = ic — reads the principle as a statement about *propagation*: the rate c drives spherical expansion of x₄ from every spacetime event, producing iterated McGucken-Sphere wavefronts on which paths, amplitudes, and entropies propagate. The standard mathematical objects of the Geometric Channel are Huygens' Principle [Huygens1690], the Feynman path integral [Feynman1948], the Schrödinger picture of wave-amplitude evolution, the Wiener-process expectation in Brownian motion [Wiener1923], the Boltzmann–Gibbs entropy growth.

None of these dualities derives from any of the others; all seven descend from dx₄/dt = ic as parallel sibling consequences. *the Algebraic Channel is the algebraic-symmetry face — sameness, invariance, group structure. the Geometric Channel is the geometric-propagation face — spread, flow, light-cone advance.* The Klein–Cartan–Noether correspondence developed in [MG-Duality, §IX] explains structurally why exactly these two faces exist and exactly how they relate.

#### I.4.4.2 The position-of-i diagnosis: why the Algebraic Channel is Lorentzian-locked and the Geometric Channel is bi-signature

A deeper structural fact follows from where the imaginary unit *i* sits in each channel [MG-Duality, §IX.12]. The principle dx₄/dt = ic contains a single load-bearing *i*, multiplying the rate c, recording x₄'s perpendicularity to the three spatial dimensions. *Where this i lives* differs between the two channels:

*the Algebraic Channel is Lorentzian-locked.* Every Algebraic Channel unitary operator carries the *i* interior: U(t) = exp(−iĤt/ℏ), the spatial-translation operator U(s) = exp(−isp̂/ℏ), the rotation generator exp(−iθĴ\_z/ℏ). The *i* is the structural feature being read as the invariance content of dx₄/dt = ic; removing it via Wick rotation transforms unitary representations into self-adjoint semigroups — propagation kernels, *the Geometric Channel content*, not symmetry representations. The *i* cannot be exteriorised from the Algebraic Channel without dissolving the Algebraic Channel entirely. the Algebraic Channel is uniformly Lorentzian: the Lorentzian signature *is* the *i* in dx₄/dt = ic read as invariance.

*the Geometric Channel is bi-signature.* The geometric propagation along iterated McGucken Spheres can be re-parameterised by treating τ = x₄/c as a real positive coordinate rather than an imaginary one. Under this re-parameterisation, the path-weight exp(iS[γ]/ℏ) (Lorentzian reading, *i* interior to the weight) becomes the measure exp(−S\_E[γ]/ℏ) (Euclidean reading, *i* exteriorised onto the τ-axis as a real coordinate). *The same iterated McGucken-Sphere expansion generates both readings.* The McGucken–Wick rotation τ = x₄/c is the exteriorisation operation on *i*: it moves the *i* from interior to exterior, from operator to coordinate.

**Proposition I.4.4.1 (position-of-i diagnosis, [MG-Duality §IX.12]).** *In dx₄/dt = ic, the imaginary unit i is interior to the Algebraic Channel (the invariance content) and exteriorisable in the Geometric Channel (the propagation content). the Algebraic Channel is therefore Lorentzian-locked; the Geometric Channel is bi-signature, admitting both Lorentzian (exp(iS/ℏ)) and Euclidean (exp(−S\_E/ℏ)) readings related by the McGucken–Wick rotation τ = x₄/c as a physical coordinate identification.*

This diagnosis is the structural reason that wavefunction collapse (Theorem X.B) and the strict Second Law (Theorem X.C) appear together as Euclidean-signature readings of the same Schrödinger evolution whose Lorentzian-signature reading is unitary. The collapse-vs-unitarity tension that defines the standard measurement problem is the Algebraic Channel reading of Geometric Channel content — the orthodox debate is the result of mistaking one face of dx₄/dt = ic for the whole. The full development of this diagnosis is in §X.14 below.

### I.4.5 The Disjunctive Forcing of dx₄/dt = ic from the joint empirical record of quantum mechanics and relativity

The McGucken Principle has been introduced in §§I.1–I.4.4 as the foundational physical-geometric primitive from which the standard formulation of quantum mechanics descends as a system of theorems. The natural question at this point is: *Why should we accept dx₄/dt = ic as the foundational primitive?* The answer developed in [MG-DisjunctiveForcing] — and consolidated in the present subsection — is the strongest available form: *the joint empirical record of quantum mechanics and relativity forces dx₄/dt = ic as a case-exhaustion theorem*. Given five empirical strands of physics that no experiment of the last sixty years has falsified, and given the McGucken-Invariance Lemma, the four-velocity budget, the Massless–Lightspeed Equivalence, the Signature-Bridging Theorem, the SO(3)/SO(2) Haar uniqueness on the McGucken Sphere, and the dual-channel architecture (§I.4.4), the only dynamical configuration of the four-manifold consistent with all five strands is dx₄/dt = ic. *Anyone who accepts quantum mechanics and relativity at the precision of current experiment must accept dx₄/dt = ic as a structural consequence.*

This is the strongest form of justification a physical principle can receive: it is *forced* by the experimental record of two foundational theories, with every alternative falsified by orders of magnitude beyond the current empirical precision. The principle is not a postulate one chooses to add to the theoretical apparatus; it is a structural consequence one is *required* to accept on the basis of empirical evidence the orthodox tradition already accepts.

#### I.4.5.1 The five empirical strands

The disjunctive forcing argument turns on five empirically settled features of physics. These are *not* features the McGucken framework introduces; they are features the orthodox tradition has established over the last sixty years through experiments that the orthodox tradition accepts as definitive. The McGucken framework's contribution is the *recognition* that these five features jointly force dx₄/dt = ic.

**(i) Tsirelson saturation $|\text{CHSH}| = 2\sqrt{2}$.** Bell-inequality experiments saturate the Tsirelson bound [Tsirelson1980] within experimental error. The empirical record: Aspect 1982 [Aspect1982] (the foundational Bell-violation experiment); Hensen 2015 [Hensen2015] (the first loophole-free Bell test, reporting $|\text{CHSH}| = 2.42 \pm 0.20$); the Big Bell Test 2018 [BigBellTest2018] (saturation confirmed across thirteen laboratories on five continents using human-randomness inputs); the Yin 2017 Micius satellite experiment [Yin2017] (saturation maintained at $L = 1200$ km separation). The bound is *saturated*, not approached — whatever entangled photons share, they share it perfectly.

**(ii) SO(3)-equivariance of entanglement correlations.** The Bell-type spin-correlation function $E(\hat{a}, \hat{b}) = -\cos\theta_{ab}$ is manifestly SO(3)-equivariant in the angular variable $\theta_{ab}$ between detector orientations. This is empirically established by the orientation-stability of the cumulative Bell record across decades and laboratories worldwide. *No systematic angular dipole in the Bell-violation strength has been detected*; the correlation function depends only on the relative angle.

**(iii) Absence of any vacuum-intrinsic entanglement-distance limit.** Bell tests at increasing separations — Aspect 1982 (meter scale), Tittel 1998 (10 km), Yin 2017 (1200 km Micius satellite) — continue to report $|\text{CHSH}| \approx 2\sqrt{2}$ within experimental error, with residual deviations attributable to detector efficiency and atmospheric scattering rather than to any vacuum-intrinsic decay. *Entanglement does not decohere with distance in vacuum.*

**(iv) Frame-invariance of c at GRB-timing precision.** Vasileiou et al. 2013 [Vasileiou2013] analysing GRB 090510 with the Fermi/LAT instrument bound the Lorentz-invariance-violation scale at $E_{\text{LIV}} > 7.6\, M_{\text{Pl}}$ (linear), constraining $|\Delta c/c| \lesssim 10^{-20}$ across an order of magnitude in photon energy over gigaparsec distances. *The speed of light is isotropic at one part in $10^{20}$.*

**(v) Self-replication of the wavefront.** Every point on a wavefront radiates secondary spherical wavelets [Huygens1690; Kirchhoff1882]. Structurally this is the iterated-Sphere content of the McGucken Principle (Proposition VIII.1 of the present paper). Without it, the wave equation $\square\psi = 0$ admits no retarded Green's function and the four-manifold cannot extend past one Planck tick. *Light propagation as we observe it requires Huygens self-replication.*

These five strands are the load-bearing empirical content. The McGucken framework's claim is that the five strands jointly force dx₄/dt = ic.

#### I.4.5.3 Theorem I.4.5.1: The Disjunctive Forcing Theorem

**Theorem I.4.5.1 (Disjunctive Forcing of dx₄/dt = ic, after [MG-DisjunctiveForcing, Theorem 8.1]).** *Let $\Pi$ be any candidate dynamical principle governing the rate and direction of advance of the fourth coordinate of the McGucken manifold $\mathcal{M}_G$, differing from dx₄/dt = ic along the rate axis (α) or the per-point Sphere-locality axis (β) catalogued below. Then:*

  *[Strands (i)–(v) of §I.4.5.1 all hold at experimental precision]$\;\Longrightarrow\;\Pi = \;$dx₄/dt = ic*

*with Sphere-surface Compton-phase uniformity. The exhaustiveness of the classification along axes (α), (β) — that no candidate principle deviates in a manner outside Modes A–E or their finite combinations — is established in [MG-DisjunctiveForcing, Lemma 2.4] and is the one hypothesis of the present theorem not re-derived in this paper.*

**Proof sketch.** The full five-step proof is in [MG-DisjunctiveForcing §8.1]; we summarize.

*Step 1 (Trichotomy of configurations).* Any candidate $\Pi$ is either dx₄/dt = ic itself or differs along one of three orthogonal classification axes: (α) rate of x₄-advance (constant magnitude vs. direction-dependent); (β) per-point Sphere-locality deviation (zero vs. stochastic vs. deterministic-non-constant vs. radial-extended vs. undefined); (γ) orientation $\pm ic$ (fixed at $+ic$ by the Generalized Second Law, Theorem X.C of the present paper).

*Step 2 (Exhaustiveness).* Every $\Pi$ differing from dx₄/dt = ic along (α) or (β) falls into Mode A, B, C, D, or E above, or a finite combination thereof [MG-DisjunctiveForcing, Lemma 2.4].

*Step 3 (Mode-by-mode exclusion).* By the table above and [MG-DisjunctiveForcing, Propositions 3.1–7.1], each mode is excluded by one of the five empirical strands at experimental precision.

*Step 4 (Mixed configurations).* For configurations combining modes that act through the CHSH expectation (Modes A, B, C), the suppression factors multiply, and the empirical bound $|\text{CHSH}| > 2\sqrt{2} \cdot 0.95$ forces the product to exceed $0.95$ — strictly stronger than the individual single-mode bounds, since each factor is $\leq 1$. Modes D (rate-anisotropy) and E (no self-replication) are excluded by independent strands (the GRB-timing bound and the existence of light propagation, respectively) rather than by CHSH suppression; a configuration combining a CHSH-acting mode with Mode D or E is excluded by whichever of its component strands is violated. Mixed configurations therefore face exclusion at least as tight as their most-constrained component.

*Step 5 (Conclusion).* Combining Steps 1–4: under the hypothesis that all five strands hold at experimental precision, $\Pi$ cannot fall into any of Modes A–E individually or in combination. By Step 2 (exhaustiveness), the only configuration consistent with all five strands is dx₄/dt = ic with Sphere-surface Compton-phase uniformity. **∎**

#### I.4.5.4 What the Disjunctive Forcing Theorem accomplishes

The Disjunctive Forcing Theorem aims at a strong form of justification: a *case-exhaustion* argument that, conditional on the exhaustiveness of the mode classification (Lemma 2.4), the joint empirical record of quantum mechanics and relativity *forces* dx₄/dt = ic, rather than the framework merely being *consistent* with that record. The structural form is the converse of the usual derivation: not "if dx₄/dt = ic, then the empirical record follows," but "if the empirical record holds — and the mode classification is exhaustive — then dx₄/dt = ic."

This converse direction is the structural significance. The orthodox tradition has accepted the five empirical strands as definitive: Tsirelson saturation by Bell-test design; SO(3)-equivariance by experimental confirmation of no orientation dipole; absence of entanglement-distance limit by Micius; Lorentz invariance of $c$ by GRB 090510; Huygens self-replication by the existence of light. *The orthodox tradition's own acceptance of these strands forces dx₄/dt = ic as a structural consequence.* The McGucken framework's claim against the orthodox tradition is not that the orthodox tradition is wrong about quantum mechanics and relativity; it is that the orthodox tradition is wrong about *what quantum mechanics and relativity already imply*. They imply dx₄/dt = ic. The McGucken framework is simply the recognition of that implication.

#### I.4.5.5 Why x₄ and not the spatial axes

The Disjunctive Forcing Theorem establishes that the rate of x₄-advance is $ic$, event-independent and direction-independent. It does not yet establish *why x₄ and not the spatial axes* undergoes this expansion. Three independent forcings settle this question, each closing the asymmetry from a different angle [MG-DisjunctiveForcing §9]:

* **Algebraic forcing (four-velocity budget).** By the Master Equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$, a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic (Appendix A §A.4), every system has a fixed four-velocity budget of magnitude $c$. A massive system at spatial rest has $|d\mathbf{x}/d\tau| = 0$ and spends the full budget on x₄-advance at rate $ic$. A photon has Sphere-tangent share v_{x₄} = 0 — the standard time-dilation factor c·dτ/dt at v = c (Massless–Lightspeed Equivalence; Appendix A (R2)) — while dx₄/dt = ic holds at every event of its worldline (Appendix A (R1)), and it spends the full budget on spatial motion at $c$. *The spatial axes do not "also" advance at c; their advance rate is the residual after x₄ takes its share*, and at rest the residual is zero.

* **Geometric forcing (Sphere-surface Compton-phase uniformity).** The McGucken Sphere has two spatial-angular degrees of freedom (parametrised by $\theta, \phi$ on the 2-sphere of radius $c(t-t_0)$) and a single radial-temporal degree (the radius growing in coordinate time). The Sphere is structurally a *record of one dimension's advance through a stationary three-dimensional slice*. If the spatial dimensions were *also* advancing at c isotropically, the Sphere would have no preferred dimension class to project against; the 2-sphere structure on which Tsirelson saturation depends would collapse into an SO(4)/SO(3) structure with different angular dependence.

* **Empirical forcing (dual-channel co-failure).** By the Signature-Bridging Theorem, the Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel produce theorem-by-theorem equivalent empirical content through structurally disjoint intermediate machinery. *Symmetrising x₄ with the spatial axes breaks both channels simultaneously*: the Algebraic Channel reading loses its Lorentzian signature anchor (the four-spatial SO(4) structure has no preferred timelike direction; $c$ becomes orientation-dependent), and the Geometric Channel reading loses the SO(3)-Haar measure on the McGucken Sphere (the surface is no longer a 2-sphere). The GRB 090510 bound and the Tsirelson saturation are *co-falsified* by any symmetrisation, with two structurally independent strands of experimental evidence cooperating against the symmetrisation hypothesis.

The asymmetry between x₄ and the spatial three is therefore not a postulate of the framework but a *forced structural feature* established along three independent routes.

#### I.4.5.6 Bohr's observation of the imaginary unit, made sharp

Bohr (collected in Wheeler–Zurek, *Quantum Theory and Measurement*, Princeton University Press, 1983) observed that *"the astounding simplicity of the generalisation of classical physical theories, which are obtained by the use of multidimensional geometry and non-commutative algebra, respectively, rests in both cases essentially on the introduction of the conventional symbol $\sqrt{-1}$."* Bohr noted the recurrence of $i$ in both relativity (through $x_4 = ict$) and quantum mechanics (through $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$) and recognized it as a structural fact requiring explanation, not just notation. He gave no mechanism.

Bohr made the pairing explicit and earlier than the 1949 essay. In "Causality and Complementarity" (*Philosophy of Science* 4(3), 1937, pp. 289–298, p. 292; from his 1936 Copenhagen address to the Second International Congress for the Unity of Science), Bohr wrote that the two fundamental constants, the velocity of light and the quantum of action, *"are introduced into the formalism as factors of $\sqrt{-1}$, the one in the definition of the fourth coordinate, the other in the commutation laws of canonically conjugate variables"* [Bohr1937]. Bohr thus named both places precisely: $c$ enters through the imaginary fourth coordinate $x_4 = ict$, and $\hbar$ through the commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$. He restated the observation in his 1938 Warsaw lecture and again in the 1949 Einstein-Festschrift essay. He recorded the shared $\sqrt{-1}$ as a formal fact common to both theories and gave no common origin for it. The framework supplies the origin: the shared $i$ is the perpendicularity of the one advancing fourth dimension, $c$ its rate of advance and $\hbar$ its action per oscillatory step, so that the commutator fails to vanish because $\hat q$ reports a location in the three spatial dimensions while $\hat p$ generates advance along the perpendicular fourth — the two are projections of one perpendicular expansion, and $i\hbar$ measures that perpendicularity and its action quantum. Bohr's careful wording is kept: $dx_4/dt = ic$ is a differential quotient and $[\hat q, \hat p]$ a commutator; the shared object is the $\sqrt{-1}$ Bohr identified, and the expanding-fourth-dimension reading of it is the framework's addition.

Two pages later in the same essay Bohr drew the epistemological counterpart of the formal parallel, and it bears directly on the measurement problem. He wrote that *"the repeatedly expressed hopes of avoiding the essentially statistical character of quantum mechanical description by the assumption of some causal mechanism underlying the atomic phenomena and hitherto inaccessible to observation would indeed seem to be as vain as any project of doing justice to the increased profundity of the picture of the world achieved by the general theory of relativity by means of the ordinary conceptions of absolute space and time"* [Bohr1937, p. 294]. Bohr paired two renunciations as equally hopeless: recovering a hidden causal mechanism beneath the statistical description of quantum mechanics, and recovering absolute space and time beneath relativity. He asserted the pairing and gave no common cause. The framework supplies one, and it is the same $dx_4/dt = ic$ whose shared $i$ Bohr identified two pages earlier: the two renunciations are the one principle read on its two integrals. On the quantum side there is no causal mechanism to recover beneath the statistics because the Born weight is the unique SO(3)-invariant measure on the expanding McGucken Sphere (Theorem 7.2) — the probability is the measure the geometry forces on the Sphere-collision outcomes, so there is nothing beneath it to find. On the relativity side, absolute rest (the three spatial dimensions) and absolute motion (the $x_4$-expansion at $c$) are real but cannot be recovered operationally, because every clock is calibrated by light and every ruler by a clock, both resting on the rate $c$ of the very expansion (the Cloaking Theorem); the absolutes are cloaked by the metrology that $c$ defines. Bohr's two vain hopes are therefore one: the statistical character of quantum mechanics and the cloaking of absolute space and time are the two faces of $dx_4/dt = ic$ — the shared-$i$ observation its formal face, the two-vain-hopes observation its epistemological face. That the measurement problem's central renunciation was paired by Bohr himself with relativity's renunciation of absolute space and time, and that both dissolve as readings of the one principle, is the sharpest historical anticipation of the present resolution.

The Disjunctive Forcing Theorem supplies the mechanism. The $i$ in dx₄/dt = ic is the algebraic record of the perpendicularity of $x_4$ to the spatial three; the perpendicularity is forced by Frobenius's classification of real associative finite-dimensional division algebras [Frobenius1878] (the only such algebras are $\mathbb{R}$, $\mathbb{C}$, $\mathbb{H}$, with the minimal extension producing a new perpendicular axis being $\mathbb{C}$ with generator $i$); the perpendicularity is the geometric content of the spherical-symmetric expansion; the expansion at rate $ic$ is what every Wick-rotated calculation in QFT, every Bell test, every GRB-timing measurement, and every photographic detection has been recording for sixty years. Bohr's observation about the recurrence of $\sqrt{-1}$ across relativity and quantum theory finds its mechanism: both theories descend from a principle whose dynamical content requires perpendicularity, and the algebraic generator of perpendicularity is unique.

The integrated identity $x_4 = ict$ is the integrated shadow of this dynamical asymmetry; the foundational content is the active spherically-symmetric expansion dx₄/dt = ic. Einstein wrote $x_4 = ict$ in 1912 [Einstein1912] following Minkowski 1908 without dynamical content; the Disjunctive Forcing Theorem supplies the dynamical content from which $x_4 = ict$ descends as the integrated kinematic shadow, and Bohr's $\sqrt{-1}$ acquires its mechanism. *The $i$ is load-bearing.*

The structural significance of the Disjunctive Forcing Theorem for the present paper is decisive. We adopt the conventions of [MG-QM, §1.5]:

**Convention I.5.1 (Spacetime manifold).** Spacetime is a smooth four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold (M, g) of signature (−, +, +, +).

**Convention I.5.2 (The McGucken Principle).** *The foundational physical-geometric primitive of this paper is the differential statement*

  dx₄/dt = ic,

*the assertion that the fourth dimension x₄ expands in a spherically symmetric manner from every spacetime event at the velocity of light, with the imaginary unit i the perpendicularity marker that records the orientation of x₄ relative to the spatial three. The integrated form*

  x₄ = ict + C,    C = 0 by source-origin convention,    so    x₄ = ict,

*is a derived algebraic consequence of the differential primitive — a kinematic bookkeeping identity, not an independent postulate. Throughout this paper, every appearance of the algebraic form "x₄ = ict" is to be read as shorthand for the underlying physical-geometric fact dx₄/dt = ic: that x₄ is, at every spacetime event, expanding at the velocity of light in a spherically symmetric manner, perpendicular to the three spatial dimensions. This primacy of the differential physical fact over its integrated algebraic form is essential. The McGucken framework is built on the geometric content "the fourth dimension is expanding spherically at c," not on the kinematic form "x₄ = ict"; the latter is the integral of the former, with C = 0 fixed by the choice of origin at the source event.*

**Convention I.5.3 (McGucken Sphere).** The McGucken Sphere of a spacetime event p ∈ M is the future null cone of p — the set of points reachable from p by an outgoing null wavefront propagating at speed c. In a 3D rest frame at proper time τ after the event, the McGucken Sphere intersects the spatial slice in a 2-sphere of radius cτ centered at the spatial location of p. The McGucken Sphere is the geometric expression of x₄'s spherically symmetric expansion projected into 3D space.

**Convention I.5.4 (Compton coupling).** A massive particle of rest mass m couples to x₄'s expansion at its Compton angular frequency ω\_C = mc²/ℏ. The rest-frame wavefunction has the form ψ ∼ exp(−i mc²τ/ℏ), with τ the proper time along the particle's worldline [MG-Compton, §2; MG-QM, Theorem 4].

**Convention I.5.5 (the Algebraic Channel / the Geometric Channel).** The dual-channel content of dx₄/dt = ic is referenced by two labels, following [MG-Deeper, §V.1]: *the Algebraic Channel* (algebraic-symmetry content) — invariance under spacetime isometries, driving Stone's theorem and the Wigner classification; *the Geometric Channel* (geometric-propagation content) — spherical expansion from every event, driving Huygens' principle and the Feynman path integral.

The six-sense identity is preserved under null-geodesic propagation.

**Convention I.5.7 (Graded forcing).** Following [MG-LagrangianOptimality, §1.4], theorems are tagged with grades: *Grade 1* (forced by the Principle alone), *Grade 2* (forced by Principle + standard structural assumptions), *Grade 3* (forced by Principle + external mathematical framework).
