**McGucken Principle anchor.** The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic states that the fourth dimension expands at the rate c, as a spherically symmetric wavefront — the McGucken Sphere — from every event of spacetime. Causal set theory is the discrete-spacetime approach to quantum gravity founded by Bombelli, Lee, Meyer, and Sorkin in 1987 \[54\]. This section states what causal set theory was created to solve, where it succeeded and where it did not, and shows that its central motivations are resolved by dx₄/dt = ic — including the two properties it most prizes, Lorentz invariance and a controlled nonlocality, which the McGucken framework supplies together from the one Principle.

**Where causal set theory started and what it was created to solve.** The program rests on a chain of results establishing that causal order is more fundamental than the metric. Robb (1914, 1936) showed, shortly after Minkowski, that the causal structure of Minkowski spacetime determines its topology and metric; Kronheimer and Penrose (1967) formalized causal spaces; and the pivotal theorems of Hawking, King, and McCarthy (1976) and Malament (1977) established that the causal structure of a suitable spacetime determines its conformal geometry — everything but the overall volume scale. Riemann (1873) and Finkelstein (1969) supplied the complementary idea that spacetime might be fundamentally discrete. Bombelli, Lee, Meyer, and Sorkin combined these in 1987 \[54\]: the causal order gives the conformal geometry (by Malament’s theorem), and discreteness supplies the missing volume by counting, since volume can be identified with the number of elements. This is Sorkin’s slogan, “Order + Number = Geometry.” Causal set theory was created to cure the three infinities of fundamental physics — the ultraviolet divergences of relativistic quantum field theory, the curvature singularities of general relativity, and the divergent result when the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy is computed directly from quantum-gravitational degrees of freedom — by replacing the continuum with a locally finite partially ordered set, so that every finite region contains only a finite number of fundamental elements and the infinities become finite.

**Where it succeeded.** Causal set theory achieved discreteness without violating local Lorentz invariance — its signature result, obtained because the discrete elements are distributed by a random Poisson sprinkling that picks out no preferred frame, so the discreteness is locally Lorentz invariant \[55\]. From the discrete order alone, its practitioners have reconstructed the spacetime dimension, topological invariants, geodesic distance, the d’Alembertian, and the Ricci scalar \[55\]. And Sorkin’s causal-set prediction of a small, fluctuating cosmological constant of order the observed value — the everpresent-Λ prediction — was made before the 1998 discovery of dark energy \[55\].

**Where it did not succeed.** Three difficulties remain open. First, the entropy or non-manifoldlike problem: if a causal set is selected by counting, the overwhelming majority of causal sets look nothing like a spacetime manifold — they are Kleitman–Rothschild orders with “three moments of time,” utterly non-manifoldlike, and they dominate by sheer number, so the dynamics must suppress them or no continuum emerges \[55, 56\]; this is, in Carlip’s words, “the manifestation of the cosmological constant problem in causal set theory,” and it is only partially resolved \[56\]. Second, the Hauptvermutung — the central conjecture that a causal set determines its continuum spacetime uniquely — remains unproven \[55\]. Third, causal set theory has a well-developed kinematics but no complete accepted quantum dynamics of the causal set, and it does not derive quantum mechanics, the Born rule, or thermodynamics; it is a program for quantum gravity that presupposes quantum theory.

**Resolution under dx₄/dt = ic: causal order and volume from the expanding Sphere.** Causal set theory takes the causal order as an unexplained primitive and must add discreteness by hand to recover the volume that Malament’s theorem leaves out. The McGucken Principle supplies both the causal order and the volume from one physical fact. The causal order is the order of the expanding McGucken Sphere: the null wavefront advancing at c from each event is the light cone, so the causal relation “p precedes q” is “q lies on or within the forward Sphere of p” — the causal structure is the expansion structure of dx₄/dt = ic (GR Theorem 11 of \[23\]). The volume that causal set theory must recover by counting is the count Ω of Compton-tick states of the expanding Sphere in the region (§6): “Number ∼ Spacetime Volume” is, in the McGucken framework, the state-count Ω of the Sphere, one Compton tick of action h at a time. So “Order + Number = Geometry” is, under dx₄/dt = ic, “the expanding Sphere’s causal cone plus the expanding Sphere’s Compton-tick count equals the geometry” — both order and number descend from the one advance, rather than order being assumed and number bolted on.

**The full Lorentzian metric, not only the conformal geometry.** Malament’s theorem gives causal set theory only the conformal geometry from order; the volume must be supplied separately by discreteness, and the reconstruction of a definite spacetime rests on the unproven Hauptvermutung. The McGucken Principle derives the full Lorentzian metric outright: the pullback of the Euclidean four-metric under the embedding carrying x₄ = ict gives ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² − c²dt², the complete Lorentzian line element including its scale, from the single algebraic fact (ic)² = −c² (Lemma 2.5, \[29\]). The metric — volume and all, not merely the conformal class — is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic, so there is no missing volume to supply by counting and no Hauptvermutung to prove: the manifold is the expanding Sphere’s coordinate integral, not a random poset hoped to approximate a manifold. The non-manifoldlike problem does not arise, because the McGucken framework does not select a spacetime by counting equally weighted orders; the spacetime is the integrated advance of the fourth dimension at every event.

**Lorentz invariance and nonlocality, together, from the one Principle.** Causal set theory’s proudest achievement is that discreteness need not break Lorentz invariance, and it discovered that the price of discreteness-with-Lorentz-invariance is a characteristic nonlocality — in a causal set approximating Minkowski spacetime, each element has infinitely many nearest neighbours. The McGucken framework provides both Lorentz invariance and nonlocality, and provides them together, as two consequences of the same expanding Sphere. Lorentz invariance is derived: the Lorentz and Poincaré groups descend from dx₄/dt = ic as theorems (GR Theorem 8 of \[23\], \[45\]), because the invariant expansion of x₄ at the rate c against the spatial slice is exactly the invariance of c that the Lorentz group encodes — the metric ds² of Lemma 2.5 is Lorentz-invariant by construction, so no preferred frame is introduced. Nonlocality is derived from the same advance: the McGucken Principle turns each local event into an expanding spherical surface, so a single local origin is physically present across a nonlocal surface at once (§5.7.4), and the entanglement and connectivity of space are the intersections of these expanding Spheres (First McGucken Law of Nonlocality, \[49\]). Where causal set theory finds Lorentz invariance and nonlocality as a linked pair — one the price of the other — the McGucken framework derives them as the two faces of the one expansion: the invariance of the rate c of the advance is Lorentz invariance, and the expansion of the local point into a surface is the nonlocality. Both are theorems of dx₄/dt = ic, obtained together, with the full Lorentzian metric and without the non-manifoldlike sea, the unproven Hauptvermutung, or the missing dynamics that causal set theory still confronts, and with quantum mechanics and thermodynamics derived from the same Principle that causal set theory must presuppose.

#### 5.8.1 Full reproduction: the static-light-cone tradition versus the active-Sphere reading, and the Sorkin–Dowker causal-set lineage (from \[29\], verbatim)

The following is reproduced verbatim and in full from the flagship Minkowski–Hilbert paper \[29\] (https://elliotmcguckenphysics.com/2026/07/05/minkowski-space-and-hilbert-space-derived-and-unified-via-the-mcgucken-principle-dx%e2%82%84-dt-ic-how-the-born-rule-schrodinger-equation-hilbert-space-lorentzian-spacetime-metric-einstein-fiel/), the corpus treatment of the causal-set lineage and the two senses of locality. It is quoted complete and unaltered.

The historical-comparison table in §1.1bis.1 catalogues a wide range of prior programs that have engaged with the null cone, locality, Lorentz invariance, or nonlocality in various combinations. The structural framing in v36 (this paper’s earlier version) characterized the Sorkin–Dowker causal-set lineage as the “closest near-miss” to identification (I), and identified the trinity-conflict-vs-biconditional distinction as the structural axis. On closer examination — with the verified primary sources read in full (Bombelli–Lee–Meyer–Sorkin 1987, Sorkin 1991, Sorkin 2009, Dowker–Glaser 2013, Belenchia–Benincasa–Dowker 2015, Boguñá–Krioukov 2025) — that framing is correct in detail but mis-located in level. The deeper structural distinction is between **the entire static-light-cone tradition of orthodox physics** and **the active-Sphere reading of the McGucken framework**. This subsection develops the deeper distinction with verbatim primary-source content.

*The static-light-cone tradition.* Across twentieth-century and early-twenty-first-century physics, the null cone of the Lorentzian metric is treated as a **frozen, passive, kinematical surface** in a pre-given Lorentzian manifold. Penrose’s twistor program (1967 and subsequent decades) constructs twistors as complex coordinates parameterizing the existing null structure of an existing Minkowski spacetime; the null cone is given, the twistors are built from it. Reeh–Schlieder’s theorem \[*Nuovo Cimento* 22, 1051 (1961)\] establishes the cyclic-vector property of local QFT algebras on regions of an existing Lorentzian manifold; the metric and its null structure are background, the QFT algebraic content is layered on top. The Bombelli–Lee–Meyer–Sorkin 1987 \[PRL 59, 521\] founding paper of causal-set theory proposes spacetime as a locally finite partial order, with the partial order encoding the causal structure of an *approximating* Lorentzian manifold — *“the metric must be Lorentzian, because no other signature than $(-,+,...,+)$ has the two-napped light cones from which the continuum’s causal order is derived”* — treating the existence of light cones as the geometric fact that justifies the partial-order discretization. The Sorkin–Dowker causal-set lineage (Sorkin 1991, 2007, 2009; Dowker–Glaser 2013; Belenchia–Benincasa–Dowker 2015; Boguñá–Krioukov 2025) Poisson-sprinkles discrete points into a pre-existing Lorentzian manifold whose light cones are taken as the kinematical given; the hyperboloid Belenchia–Benincasa–Dowker 2015 identify as the locus of $L_1(x)$ near $\partial J^-(x)$ is a region of the static, pre-existing light cone, populated by discrete points. Jacobson’s null-thermodynamics derivation of Einstein’s equations \[PRL 75, 1260 (1995); PRL 116, 201101 (2015)\] treats Rindler horizons as pre-existing null surfaces at which equilibrium conditions are imposed; the null structure is given, the thermodynamic argument is applied on it. Maldacena’s holographic correspondence \[Adv. Theor. Math. Phys. 2, 231 (1998)\] and the broader AdS/CFT literature treat bulk and boundary Lorentzian/conformal metrics as fixed inputs; the holographic identification operates between QFTs defined on these pre-given backgrounds. Light-front quantization, conformal compactification (Penrose 1965), Bondi–Metzner–Sachs (BMS) symmetries at null infinity, Strominger’s “null asymptotic” celestial-amplitude program — every one of these orthodox approaches treats the null cone as a frozen kinematical structure, a passive object that physics happens on or near or across, but not itself dynamical.

*The active-Sphere reading of the McGucken framework.* The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic of the present paper makes a structurally distinct claim: the null cone of the Lorentzian metric is **not** a primitive object in its own right; it is the *integrated coordinate shadow* of an active spherically symmetric wavefront — the McGucken Sphere $\mathcal{M}_E(t)$ — propagating from every event $E \in \mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ at velocity $c$ in the $x_4$-direction. The McGucken Sphere is an *active* geometric primitive carrying wavelength, frequency $\omega = E/\hbar$, phase, and action $\hbar$ per Planck-frequency oscillation built into its propagation. The static light cone $\partial J^{\pm}(E)$ of the orthodox tradition is the *locus traced* as the McGucken Sphere has propagated outward; the null cone is the geometric record of where the active wavefront has been, not a primitive in its own right. *The dynamics are in the premise.* (See the central content paragraph of §1.1, the inset following Principle 2.1 of §2.1, and the cascade derivation of §§2–9, packaged in Theorem 6.6.7.6.) This distinction is foundational: every static-light-cone program treats geometric kinematics as the primitive input and must add the quantum-mechanical formalism (Hilbert space, Born rule, entanglement, Bell-violation correlations) as separate structure layered on top of the static metric. The McGucken framework treats the active wavefront — and the dynamical content built into it — as the primitive, and derives BOTH the quantum-mechanical formalism AND the Lorentzian spacetime formalism of relativity as cascade-level theorems from this dynamical premise. The static null cone of orthodox physics and the active McGucken Sphere are **not the same geometric object**: the former is a passive locus, the latter is a propagating wavefront with frequency, phase, and action content built in. They share a region of spacetime, in the way that the trail of a moving particle shares a region of spacetime with the particle’s trajectory, but the trail is not the particle.

*The two senses of locality, disambiguated.* The locality discussion in the static-light-cone tradition refers to **local-Lagrangian locality**: the form of action $S = \int \mathcal{L}(x) d^4x$ where $\mathcal{L}(x)$ depends on field values and finitely many derivatives at the single point $x$. The Einstein–Hilbert action of GR, the Yang–Mills action of QFT, the Klein–Gordon and Dirac Lagrangians, and the continuum d’Alembertian $\Box$ all have this property; the action is an integral over the spacetime manifold of a density that depends only on infinitesimally-nearby field content at each point. **Bell-violation locality**, by contrast, is the no-spacelike-correlation property: measurements at spacelike-separated events have factorizable joint probabilities, the property $P(A,B|a,b,\lambda) = P(A|a,\lambda) P(B|b,\lambda)$ for some hidden variable $\lambda$. The two senses are structurally distinct: standard continuum QFT on Minkowski spacetime has local-Lagrangian locality (every QFT textbook builds the Lagrangian to satisfy this) but lacks Bell-violation locality (the empirical record of nonlocality, falsifying Bell-CHSH inequalities, has been confirmed by Aspect 1982, Tittel et al. 1998, Hensen et al. 2015 loophole-free, Big Bell Test Collaboration 2018, and every Bell test since). Standard physics is local in sense (1) and nonlocal in sense (2), simultaneously, with no formal contradiction within the orthodox treatment.

*Which sense the Sorkin–Dowker lineage addresses.* The Sorkin–Dowker causal-set lineage addresses **local-Lagrangian locality at the operator level**. Their concern is that the Poisson-sprinkling discretization scheme — which is required to preserve Lorentz invariance — produces discrete d’Alembertians whose kernels depend on infinitely many discrete events distributed on the past-light-cone hyperboloid. The discrete operator $B^{(d)}\phi(x)$ does not have the local-Lagrangian form (it does not depend only on field values at infinitesimally-nearby events to $x$); it depends on field values at an infinite set of events one Planck unit of proper time in the past. The 18-year engineering arc — Sorkin 2007 \[“Does locality fail at intermediate length-scales?”, arXiv:gr-qc/0703099\], Benincasa–Dowker 2010, Dowker–Glaser 2013, Belenchia–Benincasa–Dowker 2015, Boguñá–Krioukov 2025 — is the construction project of finding discrete operators that *behave nonlocally on the discrete substrate* but *converge to the local-Lagrangian continuum d’Alembertian* $\Box$ in the right limit. Boguñá–Krioukov 2025 \[arXiv:2506.18745\] state the engineering goal verbatim: *“This approach thus reconciles locality with Lorentz invariance, and paves a way toward defining converging discrete approximations to locality-based differential operators even in theories that are inherently nonlocal.”* The phrase “Lorentzian nonlocality” in this lineage refers to this operator-kernel nonlocality, treated as a discretization artifact to be tamed so that the continuum limit recovers standard local-Lagrangian physics. The lineage does *not* address Bell-violation nonlocality, does not offer a physical explanation of EPR correlations, and does not engage with the quantum-mechanical nonlocality of standard QM at any structural level — the quantum-mechanical formalism is treated as a separate framework layered on the causet background (Sorkin 2011 “Scalar Field Theory on a Causal Set in Histories Form” J. Phys. Conf. Ser. 306, 012017; Johnston 2008 “Particle propagators on discrete spacetime” Class. Quant. Grav. 25, 202001; Albertini et al. 2024 in-in correlators Phys. Rev. D 109.106014).

*Which sense McGucken Theorem 6.6.8.1 addresses.* McGucken Theorem 6.6.8.1 addresses **Bell-violation locality** — the structural source of the no-spacelike-correlation property that empirical Bell tests have falsified. The theorem identifies the null cone of the continuous Lorentzian metric — *not* a discretization artifact, *not* an operator-kernel property — as the structural-geometric source of the Bell-violation correlations of standard quantum mechanics. The McGucken Sphere wavefront $\mathcal{M}_E(t)$ from event $E$ propagates at null on the light cone $\partial J^+(E)$; correlations between measurements at spacelike-separated events $E_1, E_2$ in the chronological future of a common-source event $E_I$ are present in the Sphere wavefront from $E_I$ onward (Theorem 6.6.7.7 no-signaling theorem); the same null structure that the static-light-cone tradition treats as locality-supplying is in fact the nonlocality-source of the empirical Bell-violation record. The McGucken Theorem 6.6.8.1 biconditional content (null vectors ⇔ Sphere ⇔ Lorentzian signature ⇔ nonlocality) is a statement about sense (2) — Bell-violation locality — and the structural-geometric source of its failure in nature.

*The two programs are addressing structurally different phenomena that share a word.* The Sorkin–Dowker lineage works on local-Lagrangian operator-kernel locality (sense 1) as a continuum-recovery engineering problem; the McGucken framework works on Bell-violation locality (sense 2) as a structural-geometric identification. Both use the word “locality” and both invoke the null cone; the geometric objects, the physical content, and the structural claims are different. The Sorkin–Dowker “Lorentzian nonlocality” terminology is not a near-miss to the McGucken claim because the two phrases denote different physical phenomena. A near-miss would require sharing the physical phenomenon being addressed; sharing vocabulary is necessary but not sufficient.

*Why no published near-miss exists to McGucken Theorem 6.6.8.1.* The categorical structural reason is now clear: **every published program engaging with the null cone treats it as static kinematics, not as the integrated trail of an active wavefront.** A static null cone cannot be the source of Bell-violation correlations because it has no dynamical content — no wavefront, no oscillation, no frequency, no phase, no action quantum, nothing that could carry the structural information required to *produce* the correlations rather than merely *be the kinematic stage* on which the correlations are observed. To identify the metric’s null structure as the physical source of Bell-violation nonlocality, one needs the null cone to be dynamical — to have wavefront content built in. The static-light-cone tradition cannot, by structural construction, make this identification. The McGucken framework can, and does, via Theorem 6.6.8.1, precisely because the active McGucken Sphere wavefront carries the dynamical content built into the geometric primitive itself. To our knowledge, no published physics theorem prior to the McGucken corpus offers a physical-geometric explanation of Bell-violation nonlocality as the structural content of the Lorentzian metric — because the structural framework required to ask the question (active wavefront as geometric primitive) is the categorical break the McGucken framework introduces.

*Categorical novelty of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic programme.* The novelty established by Theorems 6.6.7.4, 6.6.7.6, and 6.6.8.1 is therefore a structural break with the entire orthodox tradition. *(a) Dynamical premise.* dx₄/dt = ic is an active dynamical principle — every event has an active spherically symmetric expansion in $x_4$ at velocity $c$, with action $\hbar$ per Planck-frequency oscillation — not added separately at a later stage. *(b) Active wavefront as geometric primitive.* The McGucken Sphere $\mathcal{M}_E(t)$ is the geometric primitive; the static null cone of the orthodox tradition is the integrated coordinate shadow. The relationship is one-way: the active Sphere generates the static null cone as its trail, but the static null cone does not generate the active Sphere. *(c) Biconditional structural identity.* Theorem 6.6.8.1 establishes that null vectors, McGucken Sphere, Lorentzian signature, frame-invariance of $c$, Lorentz group structure, and Bell-violation nonlocality are biconditionally tied to one another — they are aspects of one structure, not separate axiomatic ingredients. *(d) Cascade derivation of QM as forced theorem chain.* Quantum mechanics is not added as separate structure; the cascade Sphere → Hilbert → inner product → Born rule → Bell-violation correlations runs as a sequence of forced theorems from the active wavefront content of dx₄/dt = ic (Theorem 6.6.7.6, packaged with proof-level audit). *(e) Physical explanation of quantum nonlocality.* The Lorentzian metric’s null structure is identified as the structural-geometric source of the empirical Bell-violation record. This is the foundational answer to the EPR question Einstein, Podolsky, Rosen posed in 1935 and that Bell sharpened in 1964: the source of the spooky action at a distance is the active McGucken Sphere wavefront, identical to the null cone of the same Lorentzian metric that produces relativistic locality at the local-Lagrangian level.

The static-light-cone tradition, taken as a whole, was the right framework to investigate within the kinematical paradigm of twentieth-century physics — and it produced enormous results (twistor theory, causal sets, holography, BMS symmetries, null infinity, conformal field theory at null asymptotic boundaries). The McGucken framework operates one level upstream, treating the null cone as the integrated shadow of an active wavefront whose dynamical content is what generates the quantum-mechanical structure of nature. This is the categorical structural distinction. McGucken Theorems 6.6.7.4, 6.6.7.6, and 6.6.8.1 do not extend, sharpen, or near-miss any prior theorem; they state structurally new content made possible by the categorical break with the static-light-cone tradition.

## IX. The Absence of a Separate (R) Law as a Theorem

### IX.1 Proposition IX.1 (No separate (R) law required)

**Proposition IX.1 (The absence of a separate (R) law is a theorem, not an interpretive choice).** *In the McGucken framework, the apparent reduction (R) at measurement is the cumulative geometric content of four theorems: Proposition III.1 (Born rule from squared-amplitude geometry), Proposition IV.1 (superposition as geometric overlap of McGucken-Sphere wavefronts), Proposition V.1 (apparent collapse as 3D cross-section reading), and Proposition VI.1 (irreversibility from x₄-monotonicity). Together, these reduce (R) to a structural consequence of (U) plus dx₄/dt = ic. No separate (R) postulate is required, and the standard "(U) + (R)" axiomatic structure of quantum mechanics is replaced by "(U) + dx₄/dt = ic" with (R) emerging as a derived appearance.*

**Proof.** The proof is a direct combination of Propositions III.1, IV.1, V.1, and VI.1.

By Proposition IV.1, the superposition principle (SP) is itself a Grade-2 theorem of dx₄/dt = ic via the geometric overlap of McGucken-Sphere wavefronts. Multiple wavefronts can coexist at a common spacetime point because x₄'s uniform advance does not select between source events; the Hilbert-space linearity of (Q1) is a derived structural feature, not a foundational postulate.

By Proposition V.1, the apparent collapse |Ψ(t)⟩ → |s\_k⟩ ⊗ |A\_k⟩ ⊗ |E\_k⟩ observed by an observer at spatial location x\_obs is the algebraic content of the projection π\_{x\_obs} |Ψ(t)⟩, with |Ψ(t)⟩ the unitarily evolved four-dimensional state. The unitary evolution is exact; the apparent collapse is the observer's restricted access to the 3D cross-section.

By Proposition III.1, the probability that the observer's local cross-section intersects branch k is P(k) = |c\_k|², the Born rule. The probability is a theorem of the SO(3) Haar measure on the spherically-symmetric expansion of x₄ (Lemma 7.1.5 and Theorem 7.2 of [MG-BornCentury], §III.4.5).

By Proposition VI.1, the apparent irreversibility — that the observer cannot return the system to its premeasurement superposition — is the same x₄-monotonic advance that grounds the second law. The reversibility timescale exceeds the age of the universe for macroscopic apparatus, making the appearance of irreversibility practically unbreakable.

The four propositions together account for all four sub-problems of the standard measurement problem (§II.2), supplemented by the additional sub-problem of where superposition itself comes from:

* (P0) The superposition problem (where does (SP) come from?): solved by Proposition IV.1.
* (P1) The probability problem: solved by Proposition III.1.
* (P2) The collapse problem: solved by Proposition V.1.
* (P3) The preferred-basis problem: solved by Proposition VII.1.
* (P4) The irreversibility problem: solved by Proposition VI.1.

And the fifth sub-problem (P5, the nonlocality problem) is solved by Proposition VIII.1.

The standard quantum mechanics axiomatic system "(U) + (R)" is therefore replaced in the McGucken framework by "(U) + dx₄/dt = ic," with (R) emerging as a derived appearance from the combination of (U) and the geometric structure of x₄'s expansion. The axiomatic burden is reduced: where standard quantum mechanics requires two dynamical laws, the McGucken framework requires one dynamical law (U) and one geometric principle (dx₄/dt = ic). **∎**

### IX.2 The structural significance

The reduction of (U) + (R) to (U) + dx₄/dt = ic is the central structural achievement of the McGucken account of the measurement problem. The reduction is not merely cosmetic. It accomplishes four substantive simplifications:

**First**, it removes (R) from the foundational base of quantum mechanics. The standard axiomatic system has two dynamical laws; the McGucken framework has one.

**Second**, it derives the Born rule from a single foundational principle. No prior framework — Copenhagen, Many-Worlds, Bohmian, GRW, decoherence, RQM, QBism — derives Born from a single underlying source. The McGucken framework does.

**Third**, it supplies a geometric account of nonlocality consistent with relativistic causality. Bell violations and the Tsirelson bound are theorems of dx₄/dt = ic via the six-sense null-surface identity of the McGucken Sphere.

**Fourth**, it specifies the preferred basis from a concrete physical mechanism (Compton-frequency coupling), not from an arbitrary choice of system-environment Hamiltonian.

Among the surveyed frameworks, the McGucken framework is distinctive in addressing all five sub-problems (P1)–(P5) of the measurement problem from a single foundational principle, with no auxiliary postulates and no modifications of (U) — conditional on the Grade-2 status of the superposition result (Proposition IV.1, §IV.2) on which the account rests.

The structural deeper reason this is uniquely possible — and why no other framework can match it — is the space-operator co-generation theorem of §XIII.10 (Theorem XIII.I). Because $\mathcal{M}_G$ and $D_M$ are co-generated by $dx_4/dt = ic$ as a single source-pair, the McGucken framework's category structure differs from every prior framework at the foundational level. Proposition XIII.6 (§XIII.12) establishes the categorical impossibility of a separate collapse mechanism: any putative dynamical mechanism for $(R)$ would have to be (a) a new space, (b) a new operator, or (c) a new principle — and the universal derivability principles of [MG-McGuckenSpace] and [MG-McGuckenOperator] together with the inverse derivability of the co-generation theorem rule out all three. The absence of $(R)$ is therefore not a feature of the present formalism that one could imagine adding back; it is a *categorical feature* of the McGucken framework. This is the deepest structural fact behind the dissolution of the measurement problem.

### IX.3 The +ic orientation of the Schrödinger equation: a deeper structural fact

The dissolution of the measurement problem developed in §§III–IX has a deeper structural reading. The Schrödinger equation itself inherits the +ic orientation of dx₄/dt = ic and is therefore *structurally time-asymmetric*. The form-invariance of the Schrödinger equation under naive time-reversal t → −t combined with the anti-unitary Wigner operator T = K [Wigner1932] — the formal property usually adduced as evidence that quantum dynamics is time-symmetric — is a mathematical bookkeeping artifact, not a physical symmetry. This subsection makes the structural time-asymmetry explicit and develops its consequences for the measurement problem.

**Theorem IX.A (Schrödinger equation inherits +ic orientation).** *Under dx₄/dt = ic, the time-evolution operator U(t) = exp(−iĤt/ℏ) in the Schrödinger equation iℏ ∂|ψ⟩/∂t = Ĥ|ψ⟩ inherits its +ic orientation from x₄'s expansion. The naive "backward Schrödinger evolution" |ψ(−t)⟩ = U(−t)|ψ(0)⟩ is not the time-reversal of the forward evolution but corresponds physically to −ic x₄-expansion, which the McGucken Principle does not admit. The Schrödinger equation is therefore not a structurally time-symmetric equation; it is structurally one-way at +ic, and the form-invariance under t → −t + K (anti-unitary K) is an artifact of mathematical bookkeeping rather than a physical symmetry.*

**Proof.** By Theorem XIII.E, the Schrödinger equation is derived from dx₄/dt = ic through the dx₄/dt = ic Algebraic Channel algebraic-symmetry content, with the iℏ on the left-hand side being the product of ℏ (the action per x₄-oscillation cycle at the Planck frequency) and i (the perpendicularity marker of x₄ relative to spatial dimensions). The operator ∂/∂t acts on the wavefunction by translating it along the time axis, which under dx₄/dt = ic corresponds to advancing the wavefunction's x₄-coordinate by ic·dt. The full evolution equation is therefore the statement: "advancing one unit of laboratory time corresponds to advancing ic units along the x₄ axis, with the resulting wavefunction transformation generated by Ĥ."

Under naive time reversal t → −t, the equation becomes −iℏ ∂|ψ⟩/∂t = Ĥ|ψ⟩, which is mathematically equivalent to iℏ ∂|ψ⟩/∂t = −Ĥ|ψ⟩ — a different physical situation, with the Hamiltonian replaced by −Ĥ (a spectrum unbounded below, hence no stable ground state, if Ĥ was bounded below). To recover the original equation, one applies the anti-unitary Wigner operator T = K [Wigner1932], which sends i → −i. Under T, the equation −iℏ ∂|ψ⟩/∂t = Ĥ|ψ⟩ becomes iℏ ∂|T ψ⟩/∂t = Ĥ|T ψ⟩, recovering form-invariance.

But the anti-unitary T is precisely the operation of *negating i*, and under dx₄/dt = ic the i is the perpendicularity marker of x₄'s expansion at +ic. Negating i corresponds physically to reversing x₄'s expansion to −ic, which the McGucken Principle does not admit (the principle is the *physical-geometric* assertion that x₄ expands monotonically forward at the velocity of light, with x₄ = ict its integral; cf. Convention I.5.2). The Wigner T operation is therefore not a physical time-reversal operation; it is a mathematical bookkeeping device that hides the underlying time-asymmetry by formally substituting an unphysical −ic expansion that the principle excludes.

The form-invariance of the Schrödinger equation under t → −t + K is therefore an artifact of the conventional refusal to commit to a physical interpretation of the i in iℏ. Under dx₄/dt = ic, with i given its geometric meaning as the perpendicularity marker of x₄'s +ic advance, the Schrödinger equation inherits the +ic orientation and is structurally one-way. The "backward Schrödinger evolution" U(−t) = exp(+iĤt/ℏ) corresponds physically to x₄ contracting at −ic, which does not occur. **∎**

#### IX.3.1 The ontological-epistemic equivocation diagnosed

Theorem IX.A exposes a structural equivocation in the orthodox defense of unitarity. The orthodox argument runs:

* **(P1) Ontological premise.** The universal wavefunction |Ψ(t)⟩ evolves under the Schrödinger equation iℏ ∂|Ψ⟩/∂t = Ĥ|Ψ⟩, which is a deterministic first-order differential equation in t.
* **(P2) Inferential step.** A deterministic first-order differential equation determines |Ψ(t)⟩ from |Ψ(0)⟩ uniquely and bidirectionally: knowing |Ψ(t)⟩ at any time fixes |Ψ(0)⟩.
* **(P3) Epistemic conclusion.** An observer who knows |Ψ(t)⟩ exactly can therefore recover |Ψ(0)⟩ exactly. Information is in-principle recoverable.

The slide is from (P1), a claim about *how the universe evolves*, to (P3), a claim about *what an observer can in principle recover*. The two claims are about distinct things: (P1) is ontology, (P3) is epistemology. (P2), the inferential step, is purely mathematical and unobjectionable in isolation. The structural error is in concluding from (P1) + (P2) that (P3) holds for any physical observer.

Under Theorem IX.A, even the *strong* reading of (P3) — "an observer with complete knowledge of |Ψ(t)⟩ to infinite precision and infinite computational resources can recover |Ψ(0)⟩" — fails. The mathematical operator U(−t) = exp(+iĤt/ℏ) exists as a formal object, but applying it to a physical state does not correspond to any physical operation: it corresponds to running x₄ backward at −ic, which the McGucken Principle excludes structurally. The mathematical invertibility of U is not the same as the physical reversibility of the evolution. The orthodox defense of unitarity commits two equivocations: (i) sliding from preservation of the global Hilbert-space state to recovery of operationally-accessible information, and (ii) sliding from mathematical invertibility of U to physical reversibility of evolution. The McGucken framework exposes both by establishing that the principle generating the Schrödinger equation is the same principle that drives the irreversibility of the underlying x₄-expansion (full development in [MG-InfoDestruction §4]).

### IX.4 The Sommerfeld radiation condition recovered as theorem

The structural time-asymmetry of Theorem IX.A has an immediate consequence in classical electrodynamics. The wave equation □φ = 0 admits both retarded and advanced solutions; standard electrodynamics selects the retarded solutions via the Sommerfeld radiation condition [Sommerfeld1949], added as a separate boundary-condition axiom to enforce causal radiation patterns. Under the McGucken framework, the selection is forced: the McGucken Sphere expands monotonically at +ic from every emission event, and the advanced solutions (corresponding to spherically *contracting* wavefronts that would converge onto the emission event) correspond physically to −ic x₄-contraction, which does not occur. The Sommerfeld radiation condition is therefore not a separate boundary-condition axiom; it is a derived theorem of dx₄/dt = ic, with the retarded-solution selection forced by the structural one-way property of x₄'s expansion (cf. [MG-InfoDestruction §8.2]).

### IX.5 Theorem IX.B: Alignment of the five arrows of time

A deeper consequence of Theorem IX.A is that the five empirically-distinct arrows of time identified in the philosophy of physics literature [Penrose1989] — the thermodynamic arrow (entropy increase), the cosmological arrow (universal expansion), the radiative arrow (retarded radiation), the quantum-measurement arrow (irreversible measurement outcomes), and the psychological/biological arrow (memory and aging) — are projections of the same +ic orientation and are necessarily aligned.

**Theorem IX.B (Alignment of the five arrows).** *Under dx₄/dt = ic, the thermodynamic, cosmological, radiative, quantum-measurement, and psychological/biological arrows of time are projections of the same +ic direction of x₄'s expansion, and are necessarily aligned.*

**Proof sketch.** Each arrow inherits its orientation from a different downstream consequence of dx₄/dt = ic. The thermodynamic arrow inherits from the monotonic McGucken-Sphere expansion that produces entropy increase ([MG-Thermodynamics, Theorem 9]). The cosmological arrow inherits from x₄'s expansion at c being the source of the universal-scale-factor monotonicity ([MG-Cosmology]). The radiative arrow inherits from the retarded-wavefront selection of §IX.4. The quantum-measurement arrow inherits from the +iϵ prescription at every Feynman propagator selecting forward x₄-advance ([MG-FeynDiag, Proposition III.2]). The psychological/biological arrow inherits from the cumulative entropy production in biological systems, itself a downstream consequence of the thermodynamic arrow. The five arrows are therefore *not* five independent empirical phenomena requiring five separate physical explanations; they are five projections of the single physical fact that x₄ is expanding at velocity c forward, with no −ic counterpart. **∎**

The alignment of the five arrows is therefore a structural theorem of dx₄/dt = ic, not an additional empirical fact to be reconciled with the principle. The philosophical literature on the arrow-of-time problem [Price1996; Albert2000] treats the alignment as a deep puzzle requiring auxiliary postulates (the Past Hypothesis, statistical-mechanical fine-tuning, anthropic selection). Under Theorem IX.B, the alignment is forced; no auxiliary postulate is required.

### IX.6 The McGucken resolution of Maudlin's three measurement problems

The three problems of Maudlin (1995) set out in §II.4 — the Problem of Outcomes, the Problem of Statistics, and the Problem of Effect — are the contemporary standard formulation of the measurement problem in the philosophy-of-physics literature [Maudlin1995; Muller2023; Goldstein2019]. Maudlin's structural conclusion was that *any real solution demands new physics* [Maudlin1995, abstract]. dx₄/dt = ic is the new physics. The McGucken framework resolves each of the three problems through propositions and theorems already established in the present paper, with each resolution following a single structural pattern: *Maudlin's trilemmas assume that the relevant propositions live at the same organisational level; the McGucken framework supplies a structural distinction between 4D-evolution level and 3D-cross-section reading level, at which the three claims in each trilemma are jointly consistent.* The resolutions are consolidated in Theorem IX.C below.

**Theorem IX.C (McGucken resolution of Maudlin's three problems).** *The three measurement problems of [Maudlin1995] are resolved by dx₄/dt = ic through three corresponding structural mechanisms developed in the present paper:*

*(i)* **Problem 1 (Outcomes) is resolved by Proposition V.1 combined with Proposition III.1.** *The trilemma (1.A) + (1.B) + (1.C) dissolves because Maudlin's argument assumed completeness on a three-dimensional slice. The McGucken framework supplies completeness on the four-dimensional structure $\mathcal{M}_G$, with the 3D-projection $\pi_{x_{\rm obs}} \Psi$ being a derived cross-section reading. Claim (1.A) (completeness) holds for the 4D wavefunction $\Psi(x, x_4)$ on the full 4D manifold. Claim (1.B) (linear unitary evolution) holds on $\mathcal{M}_G$. Claim (1.C) (determinate outcomes) holds for each 3D cross-section reading. The three claims are jointly consistent at the level of two different domains: (1.A) and (1.B) on the full 4D structure, (1.C) on the 3D-reading projection. The collapse Maudlin's trilemma demands does not happen at the 4D level; the determinate outcome (1.C) lives at the 3D-reading projection level.*

*(ii)* **Problem 2 (Statistics) is resolved by Proposition III.1 alone.** *The probabilistic step is a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$, not a tension with determinism. Two systems with identical 4D wavefunctions $\Psi$ evolve unitarily into identical 4D wavefunctions at any later 4D event — (2.B) and (2.A) both hold at the 4D level. The probabilistic outcomes (2.C) arise from the distinct local cross-sections that different observers take: the SO(3) Haar measure on the McGucken-Sphere cross-section (Piece 3 of Proposition III.1) gives $|\psi|^2$ as the probability that an observer's local 3D-cross-section intersects a given branch. Claim (2.B) (deterministic 4D evolution) and claim (2.C) (Born statistics over cross-section readings) are both true and live at different organisational levels: (2.B) at the 4D evolution level, (2.C) at the 3D-reading projection level.*

*(iii)* **Problem 3 (Effect) is resolved by Proposition VII.1 combined with Theorem X.B's apparatus-decoherence mechanism.** *The dynamics of properties between successive measurements is supplied concretely. Proposition VII.1 (preferred basis from Compton-frequency decoherence) supplies the specific physical mechanism by which the system's post-measurement state is dynamically locked into the position basis through entanglement with environmental Compton-coupled degrees of freedom. Proposition X.6 supplies the localization rate $\Gamma \sim N\omega_C$ from the (N+1)-vertex Feynman structure, with $\sigma \sim \sqrt{\lambda_C \cdot L_{\rm app}}$ for the spatial localization length. Between successive measurements, the apparatus has been entangled with $\sim 10^{23}$ environmental constituents oscillating at Compton frequency, and the effective decoherence-rate $\Gamma \sim N\omega_C$ governs how the second measurement is affected by the first. The dynamics of possessed properties between measurements is the dynamics of the apparatus–environment entanglement, and it is specified concretely with quantitative localization rate rather than left open as it is in modal interpretations.*

**∎**

The unifying structural pattern. The three resolutions are structural variants of a single mechanism. Maudlin's trilemmas each presupposed that the relevant claims — completeness, dynamics, outcomes/statistics, effect — lived at the same organisational level (the 3D-spatial level of the standard QM formulation). The McGucken framework supplies a structural distinction between *4D-evolution level* (where unitarity, determinism, and 4D completeness live) and *3D-cross-section reading level* (where determinate outcomes, Born statistics, and apparatus decoherence live). The two levels are related by the projection $\pi_{x_{\rm obs}}: \mathcal{M}_G \to \Sigma_t$ from the 4D manifold to the observer's 3D spatial slice at observer-time $x_{\rm obs}$ (Proposition V.1). Within each level, the relevant claims are jointly consistent; the apparent inconsistencies that Maudlin diagnosed arise only when the levels are conflated, which is precisely what the standard 3D formulation of QM forces upon any account that does not have a 4D structure to project from.

This is the "new physics" Maudlin asked for: not new postulates layered onto the standard formalism (the collapse-theorist's stochastic localization, the Bohmian's hidden variables, the Many-Worlds-theorist's denial of determinate outcomes), but a deeper *physical structure* — dx₄/dt = ic, the physical-geometric fact that the fourth dimension expands at velocity c — from which the standard 3D formulation is recovered as a cross-section reading. The structural distinction between 4D evolution level and 3D cross-section reading level is the geometric content of the principle, carrying definite physical commitments (a real four-dimensional state, a real x₄-expansion) rather than serving as an interpretive overlay.

**Comparison with other resolutions.** Maudlin's 1995 scorecard against the major interpretive programmes: collapse theories solve Problem 1 (by denying 1.B) at the cost of postulating stochastic non-unitary dynamics; hidden-variable theories solve Problem 1 (by denying 1.A) at the cost of postulating non-local hidden-variable dynamics; modal interpretations fail Problem 3. Many-Worlds rejects Problem 1's claim (1.C) but faces Problem 2 in a circular form (Wallace's decision-theoretic derivation of Born requires equiprobable-branching, which itself is contested). The McGucken framework resolves all three problems simultaneously, without postulating non-unitary dynamics, without postulating hidden variables, without denying determinate measurement outcomes, and without leaving Problem 3 unspecified. The resolution cost is one new physical principle (dx₄/dt = ic) supplying a deeper structural level. By the count of auxiliary postulates added to unitary dynamics, this resolution is more economical than the prior interpretive programmes surveyed, each of which adds at least one such postulate; the framework's proponents take this economy, together with the overdetermination of Q5 in §XIII.11.1, as support for dx₄/dt = ic as a foundational principle of quantum mechanics.

The McGucken framework supplies what Maudlin asked for in his closing sentence: it supplies new physics whose structural content forces the resolution of all three of his problems as theorems. dx₄/dt = ic is the new physics.
