### XIII.16 Wave-particle duality as the dual-channel reading of x₄'s advance

The wave-particle duality of quantum mechanics has been interpreted in many ways across the history of quantum theory. Bohr called it complementarity. The Copenhagen interpretation called it context-dependent description. Bohmian mechanics retained both as separate ontological facts — a particle plus a guiding wave. de Broglie's pilot-wave theory took the wave as primary; Newton's corpuscular theory and the early Einstein photon-theory took the particle as primary. None of these treatments dissolves the duality; each takes it as a primitive of the formalism that requires interpretive accommodation.

The McGucken framework dissolves wave-particle duality entirely.

#### Theorem XIII.N (Wave-particle duality as the dual-channel reading of x₄'s advance)

**Theorem XIII.N (Wave-particle duality is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic, not a primitive postulate).** *A quantum entity is simultaneously a McGucken-Sphere wavefront (the Geometric Channel reading) and a localizable particle (the Algebraic Channel reading), with both aspects geometric consequences of the same physical fact: x₄ is advancing at rate ic from every spacetime event, spherically symmetrically. The wave aspect and the particle aspect are the geometric-propagation reading and the algebraic-symmetry reading of the same single physical fact rather than two competing descriptions. The wave-aspect identification (the McGucken Sphere as the fixed-t cross-section of the forward null cone it sweeps out, the Huygens wavefront, and the support of the retarded Green's function) is Grade-1; the full dissolution of the duality, including the localized-detection statistics, is Grade-2, inheriting that grade from the Channel-equivalence Proposition XIII.3.*

**Proof.**

**The wave aspect.** When x₄ advances at rate ic from a spacetime point p₀, the three-dimensional cross-section at observer time t is the McGucken Sphere Σ\_+(p₀) of radius c(t − t₀) centered at the spatial location of p₀ (Convention I.5.3). This is geometrically the forward null cone, structurally Huygens' secondary wavefront from p₀, and operationally the support of the retarded Green's function of the wave equation (Klein-Gordon for a massive particle, d'Alembert for a massless particle). The four are one geometric object under four names: the McGucken Sphere, the forward null cone, Huygens' secondary wavefront, and the support of the retarded Green's function. That object is the wave aspect of every quantum entity.

The wave aspect is, on this reading, the literal three-dimensional cross-section of the four-dimensional expansion of x₄ from the source event p₀, rather than a metaphor or heuristic. The wave equation governing the propagation of ψ is the equation of motion for this cross-section as t advances; the wavefront's spherical symmetry is x₄'s spherical symmetry projected onto Σ\_t.

**The particle aspect.** the Algebraic Channel's algebraic-symmetry reading of the same physical x₄-advance treats the entity as a localizable point — a position eigenstate in the Hilbert-space representation, with the momentum operator p̂ = −iℏ ∂/∂q as the generator of spatial translations through Stone's theorem [MG-QM, Theorem 10]. The position-eigenstate representation diagonalizes the position observable; the momentum-eigenstate representation diagonalizes the momentum observable; the canonical commutation relation [q̂, p̂] = iℏ is the algebraic content of x₄'s spherical advance under spatial translations.

The particle aspect is the algebraic-symmetry side of the same Klein pair whose geometric-propagation side is the wave aspect. The position eigenstate is mathematically a delta function δ(x − x₀), which is a singular limit of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront as the wavefront's spatial extent shrinks to a point — the "particle" is the wavefront localized to a single spatial location. In the position basis, the wavefront ψ(x, t) decomposes as a superposition of position eigenstates: ψ(x, t) = ∫ ψ(x', t) δ(x − x') dx', expressing the wavefront as an integral over its values at each spatial point.

**The duality is the dual-channel structure.** The wave aspect (the Geometric Channel reading: McGucken Sphere) and the particle aspect (the Algebraic Channel reading: position eigenstate) are not two separate ontological items competing for primacy. They are the two readings of the same single physical fact: x₄ is advancing at rate ic from every event, spherically symmetrically. The the Algebraic Channel reading describes how this advance manifests in the algebraic-symmetry content (Hilbert-space operators, Stone's theorem, Wigner classification); the Geometric Channel reading describes how this advance manifests in the geometric-propagation content (Huygens wavefronts, path-integral histories, retarded Green's functions). Both readings are mathematically equivalent (via the equivalence of the Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel established in Proposition XIII.3) and physically simultaneous: the same entity is wave and particle at the same time, in the same spacetime, because it is one four-dimensional object whose 3D cross-section can be read either way.

**The double-slit experiment in geometric form.** The double-slit experiment is the canonical demonstration of wave-particle duality. In the McGucken framework, the experiment is read as a literal geometric statement. The photon's wavefront — the McGucken Sphere from the photon emission event — propagates at speed c through both slit openings simultaneously, because the wavefront is spherically symmetric and the slits subtend a non-trivial portion of the sphere's solid angle. At each slit, by Huygens' principle ([MG-QM, Theorem 1]), the wavefront acts as a secondary source of new McGucken Spheres expanding from the slit openings. These two secondary McGucken Spheres overlap at the detection screen, producing the interference pattern via Proposition IV.1 (superposition as geometric overlap).

The localized detection click — the "particle" aspect — is the projection of the wavefront onto a specific detector pixel, which by the Born rule (Proposition III.1) occurs with probability density |ψ|². The "particle" is not a separate ontological entity from the "wave"; it is the same McGucken Sphere read in the Algebraic Channel representation as a position eigenstate at the moment of detection.

The double-slit result — interference pattern with localized detections — is the geometric signature of the dual-channel content: the wavefront passes through both slits (the Geometric Channel), interferes at the screen (Proposition IV.1), and is detected at one specific pixel with squared-amplitude probability (Proposition III.1, the Algebraic Channel reading). No mystery, no collapse problem at the level of physical mechanism, no observer-dependent reality. Just the geometry of x₄'s spherical advance, projected onto a 3D detector.

**Photons as perfect tracers.** A particularly sharp consequence: photons travel at v = c, which by the four-velocity-budget structure (Proposition II.2 of [MG-QM, §1.5.2]) gives v_x₄ = √(c² − v²) = 0 — a photon is at rest in x₄, its accumulated x₄-advance X₄ fixed while its entire advance is spatial and dx₄/dt = ic holds at every event it crosses (Appendix A §A.3.1). It rides x₄'s expansion as a surfer rides a wave, stationary relative to it. This is what makes photons the perfect tracers of x₄'s motion: a photon's position on the McGucken Sphere is the position of the wavefront itself, with no offset due to differential x₄-advance. Massive particles, by contrast, have nonzero share of the expansion ($v_{x_4} = c/\gamma$; Appendix A §A.1 (R2)); at rest $v_{x_4} = c$ and by the rest-frame reverse-reading equivalence (Appendix A §A.2) the chain-rule rate dx₄/dτ equals ic in the rest frame, so the particle accumulates phase at the Compton frequency mc²/ℏ.

The wave-particle duality of photons is therefore the clearest case: a photon *is* a McGucken-Sphere wavefront, with no separate particle aspect — its position on the wavefront is the position of the wavefront, with the "particle" reading being the Algebraic Channel representation of the wavefront's spatial localization at the moment of detection. **∎**

### XIII.17 The "Hilbert space category problem" addressed

The phrase "Hilbert space category problem" appears in some of the foundational literature without a fixed canonical meaning. We address three distinct readings of this phrase, each of which corresponds to a structural concern about the Hilbert-space framework, and each of which is dissolved by the McGucken framework.

**Reading 1: Which Hilbert space for a given physical system?** Standard textbooks postulate ℋ but give no derivation of *which* ℋ. This is dissolved by Proposition XIII.2: the textbook choices L²(ℝ³), ℂ² ⊗ L²(ℝ³), Fock space, etc., are forced by the geometric structure of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront for the system in question.

**Reading 2: Probability/amplitude category mismatch.** Wavefunctions are amplitudes (complex-valued); measurement outcomes are probabilities (real-valued non-negative). The standard formalism bridges these via the Born rule as a separate axiom. This is dissolved by Proposition III.1: the Born rule is the unique probability density consistent with the geometric structure of x₄'s spherical expansion, with the squared-amplitude form forced by positivity, normalization, superposition, and Lorentz-covariance. The category mismatch is not a mismatch but a consequence of the geometry.

**Reading 3: Categorical foundations of quantum mechanics.** The Selinger / Abramsky / Coecke programme takes dagger-compact closed categories as the foundation, with Hilbert space as one model among others. This is addressed by Proposition XIII.3: the categorical, C\*-algebraic, Hilbert-space, and path-integral formulations are equivalent representations of the dual-channel content of dx₄/dt = ic, with no foundational hierarchy among them. The categorical foundation is one representation of the same physical content as the Hilbert-space formulation.

In all three readings, the structural reason the puzzle arises in standard quantum mechanics is the same: the Hilbert space is taken as foundational, with the physical content unfolding within it. In the McGucken framework, the order is reversed: physics begins with dx₄/dt = ic, and the Hilbert space (with its specific carrier, scalar field, inner product, and place among representations) emerges as one natural representation of the physical content. Removing the Hilbert space from the foundational base and placing it in the theorem column dissolves all three readings of the puzzle simultaneously.

### XIII.18 Hilbert space is not uniquely quantum

A final structural observation. Hilbert spaces are not unique to quantum mechanics: classical wave equations admit Hilbert-space formulations as well. Maxwell's equations admit a Hilbert-space formulation in terms of square-integrable electromagnetic fields on spatial slices; the wave equation in optics admits a Hilbert-space formulation in terms of square-integrable acoustic or optical wavefunctions; Huygens' principle admits a Hilbert-space formulation in terms of square-integrable Green's-function kernels. None of these classical wave-mechanical systems exhibits quantum behavior, despite using Hilbert spaces.

What makes a system *quantum* in the McGucken framework is not the Hilbert space itself but three additional structural features: (i) the dual-channel content of dx₄/dt = ic (algebraic-symmetry plus geometric-propagation), (ii) the Compton-frequency coupling of matter to x₄'s expansion at rate ω\_C = mc²/ℏ, and (iii) the action quantum ℏ as the action-per-x₄-cycle [MG-QM, Theorem 5; MG-Constants]. A wave equation without these three features is classical; a wave equation with them is quantum. The Hilbert space carries both classical and quantum content; the dual-channel structure plus Compton coupling plus ℏ is what makes the content quantum.

This explains why Hilbert spaces appear in classical contexts (Maxwell, optics, Huygens) without producing quantum behavior: the Hilbert space is necessary for wave mechanics but not sufficient for quantum mechanics. The McGucken framework supplies the additional ingredients — the dual-channel structure, the Compton coupling, and ℏ — that distinguish quantum from classical wave mechanics, with all three features derived from dx₄/dt = ic.

### XIII.19 The complete structural reduction

We can now state the complete structural reduction of standard quantum mechanics in the McGucken framework. The standard Dirac–von Neumann axiomatic system has six independent postulates Q1–Q6:

* Q1: state space is a complex separable Hilbert space.
* Q2: observables are self-adjoint operators on the Hilbert space.
* Q3: Born rule for measurement probabilities.
* Q4: Schrödinger evolution between measurements.
* Q5: canonical commutation relation [q̂, p̂] = iℏ.
* Q6: tensor product structure for composite systems.

In the McGucken framework, *all six postulates* are derived theorems of dx₄/dt = ic plus standard structural commitments shared with all reasonable physical theories. The derivations:

* **Q1** (Hilbert space): forced by Proposition XIII.1 (vector-space structure from superposition, complex scalars from x₄-perpendicularity, inner product from Born-rule overlap, separability from spatial-slice geometry).

* **Q2** (self-adjoint operators): forced by the requirement that observables be real-valued combined with the action of one-parameter unitary groups via Stone's theorem [MG-QM, Theorem 10].

* **Q3** (Born rule): forced by Proposition III.1 (squared-amplitude geometry of McGucken-Sphere cross-section).

* **Q4** (Schrödinger evolution): forced by Lorentz-covariance plus the rest-mass phase factor e^(−imc²t/ℏ) from x₄-advance at rate ic [MG-QM, Theorem 7].

* **Q5** (canonical commutation): forced by Stone's theorem applied to spacetime translations, with the i in [q̂, p̂] = iℏ being the same i as in x₄ = ict [MG-QM, Theorem 10; MG-Commut].

* **Q6** (tensor product structure): forced by the linearity of Hilbert space (Q1) combined with subsystem decomposition, with the multiplicative composition of independent McGucken-wavefronts producing the tensor product [MG-QM, Theorem 20].

The complete structural reduction places all six postulates of standard quantum mechanics in the theorem column, leaving exactly one principle in the postulate column: dx₄/dt = ic. The Kolmogorov-complexity ratio is roughly 10⁴ bits (full Q1–Q6) to 10² bits (McGucken Principle), a two-orders-of-magnitude compression with no loss of physical content [MG-LagrangianOptimality, §3.1].

### XIII.20 Summary

The Hilbert-space framework of standard quantum mechanics — its complex scalar field, its specific carrier space for any given physical system, its inner-product structure, and its primacy among representations of quantum dynamics — is forced by dx₄/dt = ic together with Propositions III.1 (Born) and IV.1 (superposition), with no independent axiomatic content. Proposition XIII.1 establishes that the Hilbert-space framework itself is derived; Proposition XIII.2 establishes that each specific Hilbert space (L²(ℝ³), ℂ² ⊗ L²(ℝ³), Fock space) is forced by the geometric structure of the corresponding system; Proposition XIII.3 establishes that Hilbert space is one of several mathematically equivalent representations, naturally suited for the algebraic-symmetry channel of the dual-channel content; Proposition XIII.4 establishes that wave-particle duality is the dual-channel reading of x₄'s advance, with the wave aspect (the Geometric Channel: McGucken Sphere) and the particle aspect (the Algebraic Channel: position eigenstate) being the geometric-propagation and algebraic-symmetry readings of the same single physical fact.

The structural reduction is now complete: all six postulates Q1–Q6 of the standard Dirac–von Neumann system are theorems of dx₄/dt = ic. The "Hilbert space category problem" — in any of its three readings — dissolves into the geometric content of the same principle. Wave-particle duality is no longer a primitive of the formalism but a consequence of the dual-channel structure. The double-slit experiment becomes a literal geometric statement about the propagation and overlap of McGucken-Sphere wavefronts, with no observer-dependent reality and no separate collapse mechanism.

The McGucken framework therefore subtracts the entire Hilbert-space framework from the foundational column. What remains in the foundational column is one geometric principle: the fourth dimension is expanding spherically at the velocity of light. Everything else — the Hilbert space, the Born rule, the superposition principle, wave-particle duality, the apparent collapse, the spin-statistics theorem, the canonical commutation relation, the Schrödinger equation — is in the theorem column.

### XIII.21 The structural robustness of an empirically-anchored derivation chain

The cogenerative cascade — from dx₄/dt = ic through the Lorentzian metric, the complex amplitude, the Hilbert space, the canonical commutator, the Born rule, the uncertainty principle, and the Schrödinger equation — has a structural property that distinguishes it from a purely mathematical derivation and that merits explicit statement, with its limits stated as carefully as its strengths.

#### XIII.21.1 Mathematical proof versus mathematical-physics proof

A purely mathematical proof is a single deductive thread: axiom → lemma → ⋯ → theorem, with each step depending on the previous for its truth. A gap at any step propagates downstream; the proof either holds entire or fails until repaired. Wiles' proof of Fermat's Last Theorem is of this kind.

A mathematical-physics derivation has a second constraint absent from pure mathematics. Each theorem it produces is not only a deductive consequence of the principle; it is also an assertion about an empirically established feature of the world, validated independently of any derivation. The Lorentzian metric is the metric of special relativity, confirmed since 1905; the Hilbert space is the arena in which every quantum experiment since 1925 has been correctly described; the Born rule is the measurement statistic confirmed across a century of experiment; the canonical commutator is what every joint position–momentum measurement obeys; the uncertainty bound is saturated by every minimum-uncertainty Gaussian state; the Schrödinger equation fits hydrogen spectra, oscillator level spacings, and tunneling rates. Each theorem is therefore subject to two independent constraints: it must follow from its derivation, and it must match the empirically established fact it asserts. The derivation explains why the observed fact takes the form it does; the fact's existence does not depend on the derivation's correctness.

#### XIII.21.2 The consequence: a local break is local

This dual character has a definite consequence for how the cascade responds to a deductive gap, and it is worth stating precisely what does and does not follow.

What does follow: a gap in the derivation of any one theorem does not erase the empirical fact at that node — the fact is independently established by observation — and does not, by itself, propagate to the other nodes, provided those nodes have derivation routes that do not pass through the broken step. The superposition argument of Proposition IV.1 (§IV.2) could require repair without rebuilding the Lorentzian metric (Lemma, established independently and confirmed by relativity) or the Hilbert-space vector-space structure (which has its own construction route). In this sense the cascade is more robust than a single-thread proof: a break is local and repairable, and the empirically anchored facts remain in physics while repair proceeds. This is the structural property mature physical theories share — Newtonian mechanics, Maxwell's electrodynamics, special and general relativity, and the Standard Model have each been refined and rederived in multiple ways without losing their empirical content, because each is multiply anchored to observation rather than dependent on a single deductive thread.

What does *not* follow, and must not be claimed: that *every* conclusion is protected by a second, derivationally disjoint route. The cases separate as follows.

- *Genuinely overdetermined.* The canonical commutator [q̂, p̂] = iℏ admits two routes that share no intermediate machinery: the Algebraic Channel route (Noether on x₄-translation invariance → Stone's theorem → Stone–von Neumann uniqueness) and the Geometric Channel route (Huygens-wavefront propagation → path summation → action-quantization phase derivative), per Theorem XIII.J. Here the redundancy is real: a gap in one route leaves the conclusion standing on the other.

- *Overdetermined: the Born rule.* The exponent 2 of the Born rule has five routes that share only the Principle and the Sphere — the Conservation Route (Lemma 7.1), the Haar Route (Lemma 7.1.5), the Norm Route (Lemma 7.6), the Collision Route (Theorem 7.7, Lemma 7.7.5, Corollary 7.7.6), and the PT-Symmetry Route (Theorem 7.11) of [MG-BornCentury], reproduced in §III.4.5: "A challenge to any one route leaves the other four standing" ([MG-BornCentury] Part IX.2). The Hilbert-space inner product's quadratic diagonal ⟨ψ, ψ⟩ = ∫|ψ|² d³x is the conserved total of Lemma 7.1 ([MG-BornCentury] Lemma 7.6).

- *Single-routed.* The superposition principle rests on the empirically anchored conditions D3 and D4 of Proposition IV.1 (§IV.2). The Stern–Gerlach deflection magnitude (Remark III.4.7) is single-routed: its geometric reading redescribes, rather than independently rederives, the dynamical input.

The robustness claim is therefore narrower than "every conclusion has two disjoint routes." The cascade has (i) empirical anchoring at every node, which is the principal source of robustness and holds uniformly; (ii) derivational redundancy at *some* nodes (the commutator, the Born rule), explicitly not at others (the superposition principle, the Stern–Gerlach deflection magnitude); and (iii) multi-domain support for the upstream principle dx₄/dt = ic, which is anchored not only by the quantum derivations here but independently by the general-relativity derivations [MG-GR] (the Lorentzian signature from (ict)² = −c²t², the field equations from the curvature of the spatial sector beneath the gravity-invariant expansion of x₄ (Appendix A §A.4), the Schwarzschild and FLRW solutions) and the thermodynamics derivations [MG-Entropy, MG-Horizon] (the classical second law and its companions from x₄-expansion structure). A framework whose foundational principle is anchored across three independently-confirmed domains is destabilized only if a conclusion fails to be derivable from the principle *at all* — that is, only if every route to it fails simultaneously — not by the discovery of a single local deductive gap.

#### XIII.21.3 What hostile scrutiny can and cannot establish

This distinction sharpens what a critical reading should target. The meaningful question is whether a specific theorem fails to be derivable from dx₄/dt = ic *at all* — whether, for the single-routed nodes, the one route fails, or, for the overdetermined nodes, every route fails together. That is a physical question, and the present paper invites it: §III.4.5 reproduces the five routes to the Born rule's exponent in full so that each can be examined directly. What a critical reading cannot do is collapse the framework by exhibiting one local gap in a derivation whose conclusion is empirically anchored and, where so noted, independently routed. The empirical anchoring secures the facts; the genuine redundancy secures the overdetermined conclusions; and the explicit naming of the single-routed nodes ensures that the framework's weakest joints are identified by its authors rather than concealed from its readers.

## XIV. Why Other Born-Rule Derivations Fall Short

We now develop the comparative analysis in detail. The seven major interpretive programmes are surveyed under three structural criteria:

**(C-I)** Does the framework derive the Born rule from a single underlying principle?

**(C-II)** Does the framework resolve the preferred-basis problem from a specific physical mechanism?

**(C-III)** Does the framework supply a geometric account of nonlocality consistent with relativistic causality?

Each of the seven existing frameworks fails at least one of these criteria. The McGucken framework satisfies all three through the single principle dx₄/dt = ic.

### XIV.1 Copenhagen

**(C-I) Born rule.** Copenhagen takes the Born rule as a postulate, with no derivation from a deeper principle. The interpretation explicitly accepts |ψ|² as primitive, treating it as the operational rule for converting wavefunction amplitudes to measurement probabilities. **Fails.**

**(C-II) Preferred basis.** Copenhagen places the quantum-classical cut operationally — wherever the experimenter draws it. The cut is observer-dependent and has no specific physical mechanism. **Fails.**

**(C-III) Nonlocality.** Copenhagen treats nonlocality as a holistic feature of the wavefunction, with no geometric mechanism. The framework reports Bell violations and the no-signalling theorem but supplies no underlying account. **Fails.**

**Diagnosis.** Copenhagen fails all three criteria. It is the historically dominant interpretation but offers no foundational reduction.

### XIV.2 Many-Worlds

**(C-I) Born rule.** Many-Worlds attempts to derive the Born rule from auxiliary frameworks: decision theory (Deutsch1999; Wallace2012) requires rationality axioms whose justification has been disputed [Albert2010; Saunders2010]; envariance (Zurek2005) requires specific environmental-coupling assumptions. Neither derivation reduces to a single underlying physical principle. **Partial — auxiliary postulates required.**

**(C-II) Preferred basis.** Many-Worlds appeals to environmental decoherence to select the pointer basis, inheriting the coupling-dependence from the standard decoherence programme. **Partial — depends on environmental coupling input.**

**(C-III) Nonlocality.** Many-Worlds treats correlations as preserved across branches by the unitary evolution; no geometric mechanism is supplied for the correlations themselves. The framework explains the no-signalling theorem (different branches don't interact) but does not supply a structural account of why entangled particles are correlated in the first place. **Fails.**

**Diagnosis.** Many-Worlds fails (C-III) and partially fails (C-I) and (C-II). Its derivations of the Born rule require auxiliary postulates whose own justification has generated extensive critique.

### XIV.3 Bohmian mechanics

**(C-I) Born rule.** Bohmian mechanics derives the Born rule from the equilibrium hypothesis: particles are initially distributed according to |ψ|². Valentini [Valentini1991] showed that quantum non-equilibrium distributions are stable under Bohmian dynamics, so the equilibrium hypothesis is a separate postulate not derivable from the Bohmian dynamics itself. **Partial — equilibrium hypothesis is itself a postulate.**

**(C-II) Preferred basis.** Bohmian mechanics has a built-in preferred basis: the position basis, since hidden variables are particle positions. **Satisfies, but at the cost of assuming the position basis.**

**(C-III) Nonlocality.** Bohmian mechanics provides explicit nonlocal hidden-variable dynamics: the guidance equation depends on the global wavefunction, producing nonlocal influences on particle positions. The framework satisfies the no-signalling theorem but exhibits manifest nonlocality at the level of the hidden variables. **Partial — explicit nonlocality, but no geometric mechanism.**

**Diagnosis.** Bohmian mechanics requires the equilibrium hypothesis, hidden-variable particle positions, and an explicitly nonlocal guidance equation. The position basis is built in by hand; nonlocality is mechanical, not geometric.

### XIV.4 GRW spontaneous localization

**(C-I) Born rule.** GRW derives the Born rule from the stochastic-localization dynamics, with phenomenological parameters λ (rate) and a (localization width). The Born rule emerges as the long-time limit of the localization process. **Partial — phenomenological parameters required, dynamics modified.**

**(C-II) Preferred basis.** GRW selects the position basis by construction: the localization terms are spatial Gaussians. The cut between quantum and classical is set by the parameters λ, a. **Partial — specific basis built in, parameters phenomenological.**

**(C-III) Nonlocality.** GRW's stochastic terms are nonlocal in a specific sense (the localization at one point affects the wavefunction globally). No geometric mechanism is supplied for Bell correlations. **Fails.**

**Diagnosis.** GRW modifies (U) by adding stochastic terms, with phenomenological parameters chosen to match observed quantum-classical behavior. The Born rule emerges from the modified dynamics, but the modification itself is an additional postulate.

### XIV.5 Decoherence-plus-environmental-selection

**(C-I) Born rule.** Decoherence does not derive the Born rule. The framework explains why off-diagonal terms in ρ\_S decay rapidly, but the diagonal weights |c\_i|² are not derived from the decoherence dynamics — they are taken as primitive. **Fails.**

**(C-II) Preferred basis.** Decoherence selects a pointer basis based on system-environment coupling: the pointer basis is the basis monitored by the environment, where "monitored" depends on the coupling Hamiltonian. The framework requires specifying the coupling. **Partial — basis selected, but coupling is input, not derived.**

**(C-III) Nonlocality.** Decoherence does not address nonlocality directly; it supplements the standard formalism with a treatment of environmental coupling. **Fails.**

**Diagnosis.** Decoherence explains apparent classicality but does not derive the Born rule and does not address nonlocality. It supplements rather than replaces the standard interpretation.

### XIV.6 Relational Quantum Mechanics

**(C-I) Born rule.** RQM takes the Born rule as a postulate, treating it as the rule for one system's information about another. **Fails.**

**(C-II) Preferred basis.** RQM treats the preferred basis as relational — different observers have different preferred bases. There is no observer-independent answer. **Fails (operationally arbitrary).**

**(C-III) Nonlocality.** RQM treats nonlocality as relational: correlations exist between systems but are not features of any observer-independent reality. No geometric mechanism is supplied. **Fails.**

**Diagnosis.** RQM addresses the foundational questions by relativizing them to observers, accepting that there is no observer-independent answer to (C-I), (C-II), (C-III). This is a coherent philosophical position but does not supply a structural reduction of the measurement problem.

### XIV.7 QBism

**(C-I) Born rule.** QBism takes the Born rule as a normative coherence requirement on the agent's beliefs, justified by Dutch-book arguments. The framework explicitly declines to derive the Born rule from a deeper physical principle. **Fails (explicitly).**

**(C-II) Preferred basis.** QBism treats the basis as a feature of the agent's choice of measurement, not as an objective feature of the system. **Fails (operationally arbitrary).**

**(C-III) Nonlocality.** QBism treats correlations as features of the agent's beliefs about multiple measurement outcomes, not as objective features of the system. No geometric mechanism. **Fails.**

**Diagnosis.** QBism is explicitly anti-realist about the wavefunction and the measurement process. The Born rule is a coherence requirement on belief, not a derived fact about nature. The framework declines all three criteria as a matter of philosophical position.

## XIV-bis. Why dx₄/dt = ic Derives What Must Otherwise Be Posited by Hand: A Reply to Kinney

> It can scarcely be denied that the supreme goal of all theory is to make the irreducible basic elements as simple and as few as possible without having to surrender the adequate representation of a single datum of experience. — A. Einstein, "On the Method of Theoretical Physics," Oxford, 10 June 1933.

Will Kinney argues [Kinney2025, X thread, 13 July 2025] that three rules of physics are added by hand and cannot be derived from within a theory: that the time direction in Minkowski space encodes causal order; that the proper time along a worldline is the time a comoving clock reads; and the Born rule. He holds that demanding their derivation is a category error, since a formalism without a correspondence rule is mathematics rather than physics, and he supplies a test for the error: it is committed when one invokes quantities that cannot be measured even in principle. The objection is directly relevant to the present paper, whose central claim is that the Born rule and the collapse postulate are theorems rather than posits, and it is answered here rather than deflected.

### XIV-bis.1 The premise granted, the question sharpened

The premise is correct and is granted at the outset. A theory must posit its first principles: Newton posited F = ma and universal gravitation; Einstein posited the constancy of c and the equivalence of inertial and gravitational mass. A principle is a posit — that is what a principle is — and every theory has them. "You posit something by hand" is therefore true of all of physics and singles out nothing. What distinguishes theories is the count: how much observed physics is derived, from how few posits, without surrendering a datum of experience. That is the criterion Einstein names, and it is the axis on which this reply turns. The present paper does not claim to derive physics from pure mathematics — which would be Kinney's category error made real — but to reduce the count of independent posits by deriving, from one physical principle, structures the orthodox formalism posits separately.

Kinney's three rules are external only when the primitive is a static object. A metric of signature (−,+,+,+) is invariant under t → −t and fixes no future; a bare Hilbert space is a complex vector space and carries no probability rule. From those static primitives the three rules must be added, and Kinney is right. They are not the primitive here. Because dx₄/dt = +ic already carries a direction and a rate, the three rules are properties of it rather than additions to it.

### XIV-bis.2 The three rules as properties of the oriented expansion

**Causal order is the sign.** dx₄/dt = ic is an oriented expansion: increasing t is the +i direction of the advance, and there is no −ic branch in the physical fact, only in coordinate bookkeeping. Integrating the oriented rate yields the coordinate x₄ = ∫ ic dt = ict, the future orientation of that axis (since +ic selects the future nappe of the light cone), and the causal ordering carried by that orientation — all in one act. The causal ordering is not added to Minkowski space after the fact; it arrives with Minkowski space, because the manifold is the integral of an already-oriented rate. This is the same modulus/channel structure of Proposition II.1.2: the algebraic-symmetry content of Minkowski space is T-invariant and sign-blind on ±ic, so the forward-nappe choice cannot be derived from the algebraic apparatus alone; the +ic orientation lives in the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel geometric content of the active expansion.

**Proper time is the advance counted along a worldline.** Under dx₄/dt = ic the expansion of x₄ at rate c is what a worldline accumulates and what a clock counts. A rest mass is a standing wave in x₄ at the Compton frequency ω_C = mc²/ℏ; a clock counts those cycles; the accumulated advance is X₄[γ] = ic·τ[γ], proper time up to the factor ic. "A clock reads proper time" becomes "a counter of x₄-cycles counts x₄-cycles" — one physical quantity, carrying the same epistemic status as the statistical-mechanical identification of temperature with mean molecular kinetic energy: a physical identification confirmed by its consequences, not a derivation from pure geometry, and offered as exactly that.

**The Born rule is the measure on the Sphere.** dx₄/dt = ic generates the expanding McGucken Sphere at every event, and the Born density is the geometric content of that Sphere at a detection event (Proposition III.1). Its modulus-squared form is fixed by the squared-amplitude geometry of the wavefront cross-section (Proposition III.1, Pieces 1–3), and measurement is the pointlike first-contact collision at the absorbing event (§XI.5-bis), not an act requiring an outside observer.

### XIV-bis.3 The reduction, and Kinney's own test

Three independent posits — causal order, the proper-time rule, the Born rule — collapse to one, dx₄/dt = +ic: the sign gives the arrow, the rate gives the clock, the invariant measure on the generated Sphere gives Born. No datum of experience is surrendered; this is Einstein's criterion met.

Kinney supplies the test for a category error: it is made when one invokes quantities that cannot be measured even in principle. The Everett branches and the "measurer outside the physical system" fail this test, being unmeasurable in principle; dx₄/dt = ic passes it, running the other way. The same +ic fixes the retarded propagator (advanced radiation is never observed), sets ℏ as the action per cycle (measured in the Compton frequency and the de Broglie wavelength), and — across the McGucken corpus — gives an FLRW cosmology with zero free dark-sector parameters. The framework applies the test to itself: the foliation-relative bookkeeping quantities of the expansion are locally undetectable and are labelled as bookkeeping rather than ontology, while the physically primary primitive dx₄/dt = ic is tied to more measurement, not less.

### XIV-bis.4 Scope

All three cases are theorems of the framework as developed in the present paper and the corpus: causal order from the sign of the advance (Proposition II.1.2 and the Algebraic/Geometric Channel modulus boundary); the proper-time identity as the x₄-arc-length X₄[γ] = ic·τ[γ], with a clock realized as a counter of Compton cycles; the Born form as Proposition III.1, with measurement as the pointlike first-contact collision of §XI.5-bis. One item remains open, and it is the seed of the individual outcome (§XI.5-bis): the geometry derives that the outcome is a single definite localized event and derives the distribution over outcomes, but does not fix whether the seed realized on a given trial is hidden-deterministic or irreducibly chancy. That question is the shared, interpretation-independent residue every framework faces, and the present paper does not claim to settle it. The claim of this section is one posit doing the work of three, each as a theorem, tested by the measurable content the posit forces — with Kinney's distinction between mathematics and physics honored rather than evaded: the correspondence between a derived quantity and a measured number remains a physical identification, as it must for any theory; what the framework changes is the count of such identifications and the fact that they descend from one oriented physical advance.

## XV. Falsifiability and Empirical Discriminators

The McGucken account of the measurement problem makes specific empirical predictions that distinguish it from competing accounts. Three concrete tests:

### XV.1 Cross-species Compton-frequency decoherence (Theorem 22 of [MG-QM])

**Prediction.** The decoherence timescales for different particle species satisfy the cross-species ratio T\_{dec,A} / T\_{dec,B} = (m\_B / m\_A)² = (ω\_{C,B} / ω\_{C,A})², where ω\_C = mc²/ℏ is the Compton angular frequency. The mass-squared scaling contrasts with thermal decoherence's 1/m scaling and provides an empirical discriminator between the McGucken framework and standard thermal-decoherence accounts.

**Test.** Cold-atom systems at ultra-low temperatures, comparing decoherence times for atoms of different masses (e.g., ⁴⁰K vs ⁸⁷Rb in optical lattices). If the McGucken prediction is confirmed, environmental Compton-frequency coupling is established as the preferred-basis selection mechanism. If thermal scaling is observed instead, the McGucken account of preferred-basis selection requires reformulation, but the McGucken Principle itself remains intact.

**Status.** The signature D\_x^(McG) = ε²c²Ω/(2γ²) of [MG-Compton] is the relevant order-of-magnitude prediction, with current experimental bounds at ε ≲ 10^{−20} for Planck-frequency Ω. The prediction is testable at the 10^{−18} fractional precision now achievable with optical atomic clocks.

### XV.2 McGucken-Bell directional modulation [MG-McGB]

**Prediction.** Bell-inequality violations show specific angular signatures that depend on the x₄-phase geometry of the entangled system's local origin, beyond the standard angular dependence of the CHSH protocol.

**Test.** Modified CHSH experiments in which the angular configurations of measurement bases are varied with respect to the entangled system's emission geometry. The McGucken prediction adds a specific small modulation on top of the standard quantum prediction, testable with current Bell-experiment apparatus at high statistics.

**Status.** The McGucken-Bell modulation is a direct consequence of the six-sense null-surface identity (Proposition VIII.1) combined with the Compton-frequency phase accumulation along the particles' worldlines. Quantitative predictions are developed in [MG-McGB].

### XV.3 The conjunction of Tsirelson saturation and exact no-signaling

**Prediction.** The conjunction (i) maximally nonlocal correlations saturating the Tsirelson bound 2√2; (ii) exact no-signaling at the marginal level; (iii) the joint structure of (i) and (ii) being precisely calibrated — is, on the McGucken reading, the signature of nonlocality and the marginal probability being two features of one object, the McGucken Sphere (Proposition VIII.2). The exactness of (ii) is the exactness of the partial-trace identity, shared with the standard treatment; what the McGucken framework adds is the structural reason (i) and (ii) co-occur and are co-calibrated — both inscribed on one SO(3)-symmetric wavefront generated by dx₄/dt = ic.

**Test.** Every Bell experiment performed since Aspect 1982 [Aspect1982; Hensen2015; Giustina2015; Shalm2015; Yin2017] has confirmed (i), (ii), and (iii) simultaneously. The McGucken prediction is therefore consistent with the entire forty-year empirical record. The discriminating signature against alternative accounts: any framework that predicts deviations from Tsirelson saturation under specific conditions (e.g., very large separations, very high precision) would be in tension with the data. The McGucken framework predicts no such deviations: Tsirelson saturation holds at all separations because the SO(3) symmetry of the McGucken Sphere is a structural feature of dx₄/dt = ic and is not modified by spatial separation, while the no-signaling marginal flatness holds exactly as the partial-trace property at every separation.

**Status.** Confirmed by every Bell experiment to date. The most recent satellite-based entanglement distribution at 1200 km [Yin2017] confirmed Tsirelson saturation and exact no-signaling at separations vastly exceeding any laboratory test, in agreement with the McGucken prediction that the conjunction holds at all separations as a geometric theorem.

### XV.4 No magnetic monopoles

**Prediction.** The McGucken framework forces bundle-triviality of the x₄-phase via the globally-defined +ic reference phase [MG-Lagrangian, §III.5a]. Magnetic monopoles do not exist.

**Test.** Continued non-detection of magnetic monopoles in cosmic-ray and accelerator searches confirms the prediction. Any detection of a magnetic monopole would falsify the McGucken Principle (Level 1 falsification per [MG-QM, §1.4]).

**Status.** No magnetic monopoles have been detected to date despite extensive searches [MoEDAL2017]. The McGucken framework's prediction is consistent with the current experimental status.

The resolution proceeds through twenty-two Propositions:

* **Proposition III.1** derives the Born rule P = |ψ|² as a forced geometric consequence of the squared-amplitude structure of McGucken-wavefront cross-sections, with the three-piece breakdown (i) complex character of ψ from i as perpendicularity marker, (ii) quadratic exponent forced by elimination of alternatives, (iii) SO(3) Haar-measure shape forced by spherical symmetry. The quadratic form is derived from conservation of the Sphere's weight under x₄'s expansion (Lemma 7.1 of [MG-BornCentury]), the Born density is the forward–conjugate x₄-overlap (Theorem 7.4 of [MG-BornCentury]), and the exponent 2 has five routes sharing only the Principle and the Sphere (§III.4.5). ### XVI.2 Why this is unique

§XIV has established that, among the seven surveyed quantum frameworks, the McGucken framework is the one that satisfies all three structural criteria — derivation of the Born rule from a single underlying principle, resolution of the preferred-basis problem from a specific physical mechanism, and geometric account of nonlocality consistent with relativistic causality. The seven major interpretive programmes — Copenhagen, Many-Worlds, Bohmian mechanics, GRW, decoherence-plus-environmental-selection, Relational Quantum Mechanics, QBism — each fail at least one criterion, and most fail multiple criteria.

The structural reason is the dual-channel content of dx₄/dt = ic: the Algebraic Channel (algebraic-symmetry) supplies the SO(3) Haar measure that forces the squared-amplitude form of Born; the Geometric Channel (geometric-propagation) supplies the McGucken Sphere structure that forces the six-sense null-surface identity. No single-channel framework can supply both. The McGucken Principle is the unique foundational principle whose statement contains both contents simultaneously, and its uniqueness in resolving the measurement problem is a direct consequence.

The deepest structural reason — established formally in §XIII.10 (the space-operator co-generation theorem) — is that the McGucken Principle generates the McGucken Space ℳ\_G and the McGucken Operator D\_M as a single source space-operator pair: dx₄/dt = ic ⟹ (ℳ\_G, D\_M). The pair has full inverse derivability, so that space, operator, and principle are not three independent foundational structures but three readings of one structural fact. No prior framework — Hamilton, Heaviside, Noether, Dirac (1928, 1933), Wick, Newton-Wigner, Wheeler-DeWitt, geometric quantization, or Connes spectral triples — has a co-generation theorem. Each captured one or two of the three components but missed at least one (§XIII.13). Among the frameworks surveyed in §XIII.13, the McGucken framework is the one operating at the categorical level of source-pair generation, and the co-generation theorem is the formal expression of that fact. By Proposition XIII.6, this categorical structure makes a separate measurement-collapse mechanism impossible: there is no foundational layer at which such a mechanism could live. The dissolution of the measurement problem is therefore not a contingent advantage of the framework but a categorical feature of it.

### XVI.3 What this dissolves

The structural achievement is a *dissolution* of the measurement problem rather than a resolution. The standard "(U) + (R)" axiomatic structure is replaced by "(U) + dx₄/dt = ic," with (R) emerging as a derived appearance. The five sub-problems of the standard framework — probability (P1), collapse (P2), preferred basis (P3), irreversibility (P4), and nonlocality (P5) — are each addressed as a theorem of one geometric principle. There is nothing left to interpret: the Born rule has a derivation, the apparent collapse has a structural account, the irreversibility has a thermodynamic origin, the preferred basis has a physical mechanism, and nonlocality has a geometric mechanism. The measurement problem, ninety years after its formulation, becomes a chapter in the consequences of x₄'s spherical expansion at the velocity of light. More precisely, the measurement problem is *categorically* dissolved: by the space-operator co-generation theorem of §XIII.10, the four standard categories of system, apparatus, observer, and dynamics that the problem requires are projections of one source-pair (ℳ\_G, D\_M), and the measurement event is the geometric self-intersection of that source-pair with itself, viewed through the projection onto the observer's spatial slice. There are no four things to combine. There is one thing — the source-pair generated by dx₄/dt = ic — and the measurement event is one of its readings.

Within the broader Light Time Dimension Theory programme [MG-Proof, MG-QM, MG-Susskind, MG-Wick, MG-Nonloc, MG-Bohmian, MG-Compton, MG-Entropy, MG-Horizon, MG-Lagrangian, MG-Deeper, MG-LagrangianOptimality, MG-Cat], the resolution of the measurement problem joins the derivations of special relativity [MG-Proof], general relativity [MG-GR], the Schrödinger and Dirac equations [MG-QM], the Standard Model Lagrangians [MG-SM], the cosmological constant [MG-Lambda], the holographic principle and AdS/CFT [MG-AdSCFT], the Susskind black-hole programme [MG-Susskind], the Bekenstein–Hawking results [MG-Bekenstein, MG-Hawking], the Wick rotation [MG-Wick], the second law of thermodynamics [MG-Entropy, MG-Horizon], the Born rule [MG-Bohmian], the canonical commutation relation [MG-Commut], the Compton-coupling diffusion signature [MG-Compton], baryogenesis [MG-Sakharov], the values of the fundamental constants c and ℏ [MG-Constants], and dozens of other results — each derived as a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic.

The cumulative case is that *physics*, in the literal Greek sense of φυσική, "of nature," has a single foundational principle: the fourth dimension is expanding, spherically symmetrically, at the velocity of light. Every other major principle of physics — special relativity, general relativity, quantum mechanics, the Born rule, the Schrödinger equation, the Dirac equation, the Standard Model, the second law, holography, complementarity — follows as a theorem. Wheeler's 1983 self-excited-circuit diagram (Fig. 22.13 of *Law Without Law*) is, in this light, the heuristic image of the space-operator co-generation theorem: the U-curve is the cosmological worldline along which $x_4$ advances; the eye and the tip are configurations in $\mathcal{M}_G$; the dashed line is x₄-coincidence supplied by the First Law of Nonlocality; and observer-participancy is the cross-section reading of the four-dimensional state. The "law without law" Wheeler reached for in 1983 is, in 2026, the single source-law $dx_4/dt = ic$. The categorical claim that observer and observed cannot be separated at the foundational level — articulated by Bohr in 1934, by Heisenberg in 1955–1958, by Schrödinger in 1935 and 1958, by Wigner in 1961, by von Neumann in 1932, by Bohm in 1980, and by Wheeler in 1979 and 1983 — is, in 2026, a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the co-generation of $\mathcal{M}_G$ and $D_M$. The greats had the right intuition. The McGucken framework supplies the math.

The measurement problem and the black hole information paradox have been the two central conceptual obstacles to that unification. With their joint resolution as Propositions III.1 through IX.1, X.1 through X.5, XII.1 through XII.4, and XIII.1 through XIII.6 of the present paper, both obstacles are removed.

### XVI.bis The simple principle in the tradition of Euclid, Newton, and Hilbert

It is worth situating the structure of this work within the longest-standing methodological commitment in the exact sciences: the conviction that a great many phenomena should follow from a small number of simple principles, deductively and transparently. The present framework makes no claim to the stature of the works named below; the point is one of *method and aim*, not of achievement.

The axiomatic ideal originates with Euclid, whose *Elements* derived 465 propositions across thirteen books from five postulates and five common notions, establishing the deductive model that has governed mathematical reasoning for more than two millennia and whose logical rigor was not surpassed until the nineteenth century. The decisive feature was structural: an entire science erected on a handful of assumptions "so simple that they need no" defense, with every subsequent result traced back to them.

Newton inherited this ideal directly. He cast the *Principia* in Euclidean form — calling his laws of motion "axioms" and deducing universal gravitation as theorems — and stated the governing aesthetic plainly: in Book III, "Nature is pleased with simplicity, and affects not the pomp of superfluous causes," and elsewhere, "it is the glory of geometry that from so few principles it can accomplish so much." Steven Weinberg, surveying the same tradition three centuries later, judged that "it is with Isaac Newton that the modern dream of a final theory really begins." The method and the dream are one: few principles, many consequences, all connected.

Hilbert made the program explicit for physics. His *Grundlagen der Geometrie* (1899) re-founded geometry on an independent, complete axiom set, and the sixth of his 1900 problems called for "the mathematical treatment of the axioms of physics" — to treat the physical sciences "in the same manner, by means of axioms," as geometry. Hilbert's own criterion of a good axiom was that it "contain no more than a single idea." His engagement with this problem spanned 1894 to 1932, and along the way he contributed both the variational form of general relativity (the Einstein–Hilbert action) and the functional-analytic arena of quantum mechanics (Hilbert space) — the very structures the present paper takes as its subject. Einstein, pursuing the same conviction in his decades-long search for a unified field theory, held that the success of the method "justifies us in believing that nature is the realization of the simplest conceivable mathematical ideas," consciously echoing Newton's "Nature is pleased with simplicity."

The present framework stands in this methodological line. Its single innovation is interpretive rather than mathematical: the term x₄ in dx₄/dt = ic is read not as a static imaginary coordinate but as a *nonlocal spherical wavefront expanding at the velocity of light from every event*. The integrated coordinate x₄ = ict is, on this reading, the mere kinematic shadow of the active expansion. That one reinterpretation is what drives the derivations of this paper and its companions: the Lorentzian signature, the complex amplitude, the Hilbert space, the Born rule, the measurement structure, and — across the broader corpus — the Einstein field equations and the classical second law. The mathematics at each step is largely standard; what is new is the geometric-physical premise from which the standard mathematics is made to descend. This is the same move Euclid, Newton, and Hilbert each made in their own domain: not to invent new machinery at every turn, but to find the one principle from which the existing machinery follows.

It is also worth stating why this aim is not idiosyncratic but central. The reductionist program — Weinberg's "grand reductionism," "the view that scientific principles can all be in principle traced down to a small body of simple universal laws" — has been the organizing ambition of theoretical physics since Newton, and the unification of separate domains under common principles (electricity, magnetism, and optics under Maxwell; space, time, and gravitation under Einstein; the electroweak unification for which Weinberg shared the 1979 Nobel) is its recurring signature. The observation that gravitation, quantum mechanics, and thermodynamics describe one and the same universe is itself a reason to expect common foundational rules to underlie all three; seeking those rules is the stated goal of the unification program. The philosophy of physics, in its turn, when it sets aside instrumentalism to ask after the *ontology* — what the world must be like for the equations to hold — pursues the same end by a different road: not merely to predict, but to identify the underlying structure that makes the predictions true. The present framework's claim is modest in stature and specific in content: that a single geometric principle about the expansion of the fourth dimension supplies, as theorems, structures that the orthodox tradition has had to postulate — and that this is the kind of result the tradition from Euclid to Weinberg has always sought. Whether the claim survives scrutiny is, properly, for that scrutiny to determine; §III.4.5 and §XIII.21 set out the derivation routes and the open questions for it.

The canonical statement of the standard mathematical formulation of quantum mechanics is the Dirac–von Neumann axiom system [Dirac1930; vonNeumann1932], freely available in its contemporary canonical form as the Wikipedia article *Mathematical formulation of quantum mechanics* [WikiQM2026]. That article enumerates approximately ten foundational postulates as the standard formulation of QM. *Every one of those postulates is recovered in the present paper as a derived theorem of dx₄/dt = ic.* The cross-walk is consolidated below; its formal expanded version is given in Appendix B.

The structural advantage is that the McGucken framework does not replace the canonical Dirac–von Neumann formulation as represented on the Wikipedia article [WikiQM2026]; it *derives* it. The standard machinery — Hilbert space, Hermitian operators, the Schrödinger equation, the Born rule, unitary evolution, partial trace, POVMs, Stone's theorem, spin-statistics, the no-signaling theorem — is retained without modification. What changes is the foundational layer. The standard formulation is the *the Algebraic Channel* algebraic shadow of the *the Geometric Channel* geometric content carried by dx₄/dt = ic (cf. dual-channel architecture, Theorems XIII.A–XIII.N). The postulates of the standard formulation are not abandoned; they are *explained*.

This is the rigorous physical content behind the McGucken philosophy: the philosophy is rooted in physics. The formalism of quantum mechanics — every line of the Wikipedia article [WikiQM2026] — is a downstream consequence of the single physical-geometric fact that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light from every spacetime event. dx₄/dt = ic is not an axiom, not a postulate, not an interpretive choice, and not a metaphor: it is the physical primitive from which the standard formulation of quantum mechanics descends as a system of theorems.

Newton was right that something physically primary stands behind clock-time. He named it *absolute, true, mathematical time*. Einstein corrected the details — the *coordinate* time $t$ of clocks is observer-dependent — while preserving the intuition that *something* about temporal becoming had to be primary, an inseparable connection between time and the signal velocity. Wheeler warned that "time is in trouble" and asked for a deeper structure. The McGucken Principle is that structure: it does not abandon Newton's absolute time but vindicates it, relocating it from the coordinate $t$ of clocks (which the twentieth century correctly recognized was not absolute) to the *rate* $dx_4/dt$ at which the fourth dimension expands (which is absolute, at every event, in every frame, in every gravitational potential). The time we measure on our watches and clocks are but shadows of the light cast by dx₄/dt = ic in various caves — quantum mechanics, general relativity, thermodynamics, cosmology, biology — and the structural payoff of the present paper is the recognition, in each cave, that the local shadow is derivative of the same fire that casts the shadows in every other cave. The McGucken framework is what becomes possible when the prisoner is released from the cave (§I.4.3).

## Appendix A. Reading the McGucken Principle: A Note on $dx_4/dt$, $dx_4/d\tau$, and the Photon — Clarifying Common Reader Misconceptions

*About this appendix.* Readers arriving at the McGucken Principle from a standard graduate-relativity background bring one deep habit: the reflex to treat per-proper-time quantities as the "physical" or "covariant" ones, and per-coordinate-time quantities as gauge-dependent bookkeeping. That habit points the wrong way here, because the Principle is a statement about the manifold itself — an expansion happening at every event, at the same rate, regardless of which worldline crosses that event. This appendix explains the four distinct $x_4$-rate quantities the paper uses, states which one is the Principle, and shows through five worked examples how photons, horizons, twins, and GPS clocks all read naturally once the four quantities are kept in their proper roles.

### A.0 The Physical Fact

Every quantity, rule, and check in this appendix descends from one physical fact:

> The fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding in a spherically symmetric manner at the rate of $c$ from every spacetime event, or $dx_4/dt = ic$.

That is the McGucken Principle. Before any of its consequences are unpacked, its status must be stated plainly, because it is the point on which every reading in this appendix turns: $dx_4/dt = ic$ is an ontological claim — a statement about what physically is — and not a coordinate convention, a formal device, or a notational choice. It asserts that the fourth dimension is a real dimension that is really expanding, at the rate $c$, from every event of spacetime, now. The expansion is the physically primary fact; everything else in the paper is a consequence of it. Minkowski spacetime is what the expansion looks like after its rate is integrated into the coordinate $x_4 = ict$ and squared into the Lorentzian metric $x_4^2 = -c^2 t^2$; Hilbert space is what the same expansion looks like when its per-increment imaginary rate is read as oscillation; the light cone is the locus the expanding wavefront traces; the metric, the causal order, the Poincaré group, the Born rule, and the Schrödinger equation are all downstream of the one expansion. None of these is postulated independently. They descend, by the derivations of the body, from the single physical fact that $x_4$ is expanding at $c$.

This is the reversal the reader must hold onto throughout. Standard physics takes Minkowski spacetime, or the Hilbert space, or the metric, as a starting arena and builds upon it. Here the arena is not a starting point but a result: the starting point is the physical expansion $dx_4/dt = ic$, and the arena is what that expansion generates. When the appendix below insists that $dx_4/dt = ic$ is primary and the per-proper-time quantities are constructed from it, this is what is meant — not a preference among equivalent formalisms, but a claim about which fact is physically prior. The rate is prior; the worldlines that share in it, the metric that its squaring produces, and the observers that read it are all posterior.

The imaginary unit $i$ in $dx_4/dt = ic$ records the algebraic perpendicularity of the $x_4$-axis to the three spatial axes on which the expansion casts its projection. Its geometric realisation at each event $p \in \mathcal{M}_G$ is the McGucken Sphere $M_p^+(t)$ — the spherical wavefront of radius $ct$ swept out around $p$ by the $x_4$-expansion. The Sphere is what distinguishes the Principle from Minkowski's constant four-velocity norm $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$: the norm is a scalar constraint carrying no group action and no measure, and it survives here as a theorem of the Principle (the chain-rule pullback of the Sphere's expansion rate).

The Sphere carries structure that supplies the Born rule downstream by five independent routes, established in the body of the paper and consolidated here. The two most fundamental are the Metric Route (the exponent 2 is the rank of the Minkowski metric that $x_4 = ict$ induces; Lemma 7.1) and the Haar Route (the Sphere's transitive $SO(3)$ action forces a unique invariant probability measure; Lemma 7.1.5). That these structurally-disjoint derivations return the same Born density $|\psi|^2$ is an instance of the convergent overdetermination catalogued in Remark 7.17 and §17.5bis; see Remark A.0.1.

**Remark A.0.1 (Five independent derivations of the Born rule).** The Born density $P = |\psi|^2$ is derived in this framework by five routes that share no premises beyond the McGucken Sphere itself, each proceeding from a distinct property of the one Sphere. They are given here in order of foundational priority, matching the catalogue of Remark 7.17.

(1) *Metric Route* — the Sphere's metric rank (Lemma 7.1; Theorem 7.2). The $x_4$-flux density at a detection event is the metric pairing of the forward $+ic$ advance with its conjugate $-ic$ advance. The Minkowski metric induced by $x_4 = ict$ is a rank-2 tensor, so the pairing is bilinear in $(\psi, \psi^*)$; rank-4 quartic densities are excluded by rank-counting, and $U(1)$ phase invariance, reality, non-negativity, and normalization then force $P = |\psi|^2$ uniquely. The exponent 2 is the rank of the metric. This is the most fundamental route, because the exponent is a property of the metric the Principle itself induces.

(2) *Haar Route* — the Sphere's symmetry group (Lemma 7.1.5). The Sphere at the detection event is a round $S^2 \cong SO(3)/SO(2)$ carrying the transitive $SO(3)$ action fixed by the isotropy of the $x_4$-expansion. By the uniqueness of the invariant measure on a homogeneous space of a compact group, there is exactly one $SO(3)$-invariant probability measure on the Sphere, the round measure $d\mu = \sin\theta\, d\theta\, d\phi / (4\pi)$, and this is the Born weight over detection directions. This is the route that answers why a probability measure exists at all: a measure is physically forced only where a symmetry singles it out uniquely, and $SO(3)$ singles out exactly this one. Minkowski's norm $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ carries no group action and therefore no such measure — which is why the Sphere, not the bare norm, is what grounds quantum probability.

(3) *Norm Route* — the Sphere's sesquilinear inner product (Lemma 7.6). The rank-2 sesquilinear inner product satisfies the parallelogram identity as a two-line algebraic consequence, giving the L²-norm structure on Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ with no Jordan–von Neumann theorem needed as upstream input.

(4) *Collision Route* — two physical Spheres (Theorem 7.7; Lemma 7.7.5). The number of physical participants in a head-on detection event is exactly two — emitter Sphere and absorber Sphere — and the coincidence rate is sesquilinear in the two amplitudes, with sum, max, min, and arithmetic/geometric/harmonic means excluded by action-additivity.

(5) *PT-Symmetry Route* — the Sphere's reflection (Theorem 7.11). The Sphere's discrete $PT_E$-symmetry through its source event gives $\psi^*(P) = \psi(PT_E \cdot P)$ exactly, so the squaring in the Born density is the cascade-level expression of that symmetry, and complex conjugation itself is grounded in it.

Routes (1) and (2) proceed respectively from the rank of the metric and the symmetry group of the Sphere, and are foregrounded as the two most important: the first fixes the exponent as the metric's rank, the second supplies the invariant measure a probability rule requires. Routes (3)–(5) confirm the same exponent from the norm, the physical collision count, and the reflection symmetry. No route uses another's premise — rank 2, the $SO(3)$ action, the parallelogram identity, the two-participant count, and the PT-reflection are five logically independent facts about the same Sphere — so their agreement on $P = |\psi|^2$ is genuine convergence, not one argument told five times. This is the sense in which the Born rule is convergently overdetermined by $dx_4/dt = ic$ (Remark 7.17; §17.5bis): one downstream fact fixed by five upstream properties of the Sphere.

### A.1 The Four $x_4$-Rate Quantities

The framework uses four related quantities associated with the fourth dimension's advance. Each has its own symbol, its own domain of definition, and its own interpretation, and they diverge on null worldlines.

**(R1) The coordinate rate $dx_4/dt = ic$**, parameter: coordinate $t$; range: fixed value $ic$; universal — holds at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$. *The Principle.* With the integrated shadow $x_4 = ict$, this rate holds identically along every worldline of $\mathcal{M}_G$ — timelike, null, accelerated, at any gravitational potential — because $x_4$ is a coordinate function of $t$ alone. Every statement about the universality of the expansion, its metric-independence (GR T2), or its exception-freeness is a statement in (R1).

**(R2) The Sphere-tangent velocity component $v_{x_4} \equiv \sqrt{c^2 - v^2}$** (the worldline's share of the $x_4$-expansion, per coordinate time); parameter: coordinate $t$; range: $[0, c]$; worldline-dependent. A bounded quantity (Lemma 5.1.3.2). The partition $v^2 + v_{x_4}^2 = c^2$ holds for every worldline, null ones included: at spatial rest $v_{x_4} = c$; on a null worldline $v = c$ gives $v_{x_4} = 0$. On timelike worldlines, $v_{x_4}$ coincides with the standard time-dilation-related quantities of special relativity: $v_{x_4} = c\, d\tau/dt = c/\gamma$ for $0 \le v < c$. The identity $v_{x_4} = c\, d\tau/dt$ is a theorem about $v_{x_4}$ — $\tau$ appears as output, not as the differentiation parameter. At $v = c$ (the null limit) all three expressions give $v_{x_4} = 0$: the $\sqrt{c^2 - v^2}$ form by direct substitution, the $c\, d\tau/dt$ form as the ratio $c \cdot 0/dt$ with $d\tau = 0$, and the $c/\gamma$ form as the limit $\gamma \to \infty$. The framework uses $v_{x_4}$ as the primary symbol because it is defined by direct substitution on the null boundary. Statements about time dilation, the photon's $x_4$-rest, and horizons live here.

**(R3) The Lorentzian temporal component $u^4 = dx_4/d\tau = ic\gamma$**; parameter: proper $\tau$; unbounded, undefined on null worldlines; a chain-rule consequence. Derived from (R1) by the chain rule (Theorem 5.1.2.8): $dx_4/d\tau = (dx_4/dt)(dt/d\tau) = ic\gamma$. Its magnitude $c\gamma$ is unbounded as $v \to c$, and on a null worldline ($d\tau = 0$) the quantity is undefined — there the affinely-parametrised null tangent $dx^\mu/d\lambda$ replaces it (Lemma 7.2.2.1a).

**(R4) The accumulated $x_4$-advance along $\gamma$, $X_4[\gamma] \equiv \int_\gamma ic\, d\tau = ic\, \tau[\gamma]$**; a worldline functional, path-dependent. Distinct from the coordinate $x_4$. Two worldlines sharing endpoints share $\Delta x_4 = ic\, \Delta t$ but generally differ in $X_4$. Along a null worldline $X_4$ is constant; around any closed curve $\oint dx_4 = 0$ identically. Statements about differential aging (the twins) live in (R4). The bridge to (R2): $dX_4 = ic\, d\tau = i\, v_{x_4}\, dt$.

### A.2 Which One Is the Principle

The Principle is $dx_4/dt = ic$: the coordinate-time reading (R1). Because $x_4$ is a coordinate function of $t$ alone, the rate $dx_4/dt$ takes the same value $ic$ at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$ — an expanding photon-event, a horizon event, an event on any accelerated worldline. The reading $dx_4/d\tau = ic$ is available too, but only where $d\tau = dt$: on a worldline at spatial rest, the chain rule collapses and (R1) coincides with the value of (R3). This is Lemma 4.7 (the rest-frame reverse-reading equivalence), and the qualification $d\tau = dt$ is what makes it valid. On a moving worldline the chain rule gives $ic\gamma$; on a null worldline the quantity does not exist. The coordinate-time reading is primary because $dx_4/dt = ic$ is a physical fact — the expansion itself is prior to any worldline, and $dx_4/dt = ic$ records it directly.

### A.3 Reading the Photon, the Horizon, and the Time-Dilation Formula

**A.3.1 What is the photon's $x_4$-rate?** The photon's share in the expansion is zero: $v_{x_4} = 0$ (the $v = c$ limit of $v^2 + v_{x_4}^2 = c^2$), obtained by direct substitution of $v = c$ into $v_{x_4} = \sqrt{c^2 - v^2}$. The reader may be tempted to write "$dx_4/dt = 0$ for the photon" or "$dx_4/d\tau = 0$." Neither is available. The first is the coordinate rate (R1), which is $ic$ at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$ including the photon's — what vanishes is the photon's share, not the expansion. The second is $0/0$: proper time is not defined for a photon ($d\tau = 0$ pointwise). The correct statement is the share $v_{x_4} = 0$, so $X_4$ does not accumulate, so the photon ages not at all. The Principle continues to hold at every event the photon crosses.

**A.3.2 What does "the $x_4$-rate at the horizon" mean?** The rate is gravity-rigid: $\partial(dx_4/dt)/\partial g_{\mu\nu} = 0$ (GR T2). The rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ takes the same value near the horizon as at infinity. What varies with potential is the share: $v_{x_4}(r) = c\, d\tau/dt = c\sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$ (static Schwarzschild observer), vanishing at $r = r_s$. On the infaller's own clock $d\tau = dt$ locally and Lemma 4.7 applies: the local rate is the full $ic$ throughout. Gravitational time dilation is the coordinate-frame projection of a locally invariant rate.

**A.3.3 Which identity is "$c^2$ through spacetime"?** Sphere partition (per coordinate time, all worldlines): $v^2 + v_{x_4}^2 = c^2$, bounded, locus a quarter-circle. Lorentzian four-velocity norm (per proper time, massive worldlines): $u^\mu u_\mu = |dx_4/d\tau|^2 - |d\vec x/d\tau|^2 = -c^2$, unbounded in each term, signature difference fixing the invariant. The Euclidean per-proper-time sum $|dx_4/d\tau|^2 + |d\vec x/d\tau|^2$ equals $c^2$ only in the instantaneous rest frame; elsewhere $c^2\gamma^2$. Plus-sign identities belong to (R2); minus-sign identities to (R3).

**A.3.4 How does the twin paradox read?** Coordinate accumulation is path-independent: both twins accumulate $\Delta x_4 = ic\, \Delta t$. Differential ageing is read from $X_4 = \int ic\, d\tau$, advancing at real magnitude $v_{x_4}$ per unit coordinate time. On the traveling leg $v_{x_4} < c$, so the traveler accumulates less $X_4$, so less proper time. The stay-at-home twin retains $v_{x_4} = c$ and accumulates the maximal $X_4$. The CTC question closes the same way: $\oint dx_4 = 0$ identically, so a CTC cannot run on the coordinate; the impossibility lives in $X_4$.

**A.3.5 $\gamma$-projection and rapidity.** A boost is hyperbolic: rapidity $\phi$ with $\cosh\phi = \gamma$. The Sphere-partition projection is circular: Sphere angle $\theta$ with $\sin\theta = v/c$, $\cos\theta = v_{x_4}/c = 1/\gamma$. Related by the Gudermannian, $\theta = \mathrm{gd}(\phi)$, so $\cos\theta = \mathrm{sech}\,\phi$. The $1/\gamma$ projection is about $\theta$; unbounded component growth is about $\phi$.

### A.4 Why Nothing of Relativity Is Lost

The fourth dimension advances at the same rate at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$; worldlines differ only in how much of that advance they share in. Massive at rest shares fully ($v_{x_4} = c$); moving shares less ($v_{x_4} = \sqrt{c^2 - v^2}$, clock slowed by the Lorentz factor); photon does not share at all ($v_{x_4} = 0$, ageless, no $X_4$). Lorentz invariance survives entire because the invariant content — the norm $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ and the metric — is a theorem of the Principle (the metric is the pullback of the Euclidean form along $x_4 = ict$, the $-c^2$ from $(ic)^2$). Lorentz transformations preserve that derived metric; $\gamma$, time dilation, length contraction, $E = \gamma mc^2$, the null cone, and the mass-shell all come out unchanged. The foliation quantities $v_{x_4}$ and $X_4$ are additional bookkeeping frame-anchored to the cosmic-comoving foliation (the CMB rest frame); the Cloaking Theorem (Theorem 39) explains why local metrology cannot detect them. GR survives by the invariant/deformable split: the rate is gravity-rigid; gravity deforms the spatial sector. Time dilation, redshift, light bending, perihelion advance, the horizon, and the field equations are recovered exactly. The horizon is where the share is extinguished; the expansion does not stop.

### A.5 Worked Examples

**A.5.1 The twin paradox.** Traveler at speed $v$ for coordinate time $\Delta t$. Coordinate accumulation: $\Delta x_4 = ic\, \Delta t$ for both. Traveler's share: $v_{x_4} = c\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$. Accumulated: $\Delta X_4^{\rm trav} = ic\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}\, \Delta t$ vs $\Delta X_4^{\rm stay} = ic\, \Delta t$. Differential aging: $\Delta\tau^{\rm trav} - \Delta\tau^{\rm stay} = \Delta t\,(\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2} - 1) < 0$: the traveler is younger by exactly the Lorentz factor.

**A.5.2 GPS clock rate.** Satellite at radius $r$, speed $v$, mass $M$. Principle: $dx_4/dt = ic$. Gravitational share: $v_{x_4}^{\rm grav}/c = \sqrt{1 - 2GM/rc^2}$; kinematic factor $\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$. Total: $v_{x_4}^{\rm sat}/c \approx 1 - GM/(rc^2) - v^2/(2c^2)$. Ground: $\approx 1 - GM/(R_\oplus c^2)$. Fractional difference $\approx GM(1/R_\oplus - 1/r) - v^2/(2c^2)$, matching the $+4.5 \times 10^{-10}$ pre-launch offset at $r = 26{,}600$ km, $v = 3.87$ km/s.

**A.5.3 Schwarzschild gravitational redshift.** Photon from $r_1$ to $r_2 > r_1$. Principle: $dx_4/dt = ic$. Local clock rate: $v_{x_4}(r)/c = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$. Frequency ratio $\nu_2/\nu_1 = \sqrt{(1 - r_s/r_1)/(1 - r_s/r_2)}$; weak-field $\Delta\nu/\nu \approx -GM(1/r_2 - 1/r_1)/c^2$, matching Pound–Rebka 1959. Photon: $v_{x_4} = 0$ throughout, no $X_4$. The redshift is about the clock rates at emitter and receiver, not the photon.

**A.5.4 Hawking temperature.** At $r = r_s$, local share $v_{x_4}(r) \to 0$. Surface gravity $\kappa = c/(2r_s)$; compactification circumference $L_H = 4\pi r_s = c\hbar\beta_H$; temperature $T_H = \hbar c^3/(8\pi GM k_B)$. The expansion does not stop at the horizon; the share is extinguished on the static foliation, and compactification of the Euclidean-section $x_4$-axis at $L_H$ produces the thermal spectrum.

**A.5.5 Bell's spaceship.** Rockets $A, B$ at proper distance $L_0$, accelerating identically. Coordinate rate: $dx_4/dt = ic$. Share: $v_{x_4}(t) = c\sqrt{1 - v(t)^2/c^2}$, decreasing. Accumulated: $X_4^A = X_4^B$, so both age identically. Launch-frame separation constant $L_0$; co-moving separation $L(t) = L_0\, c/v_{x_4}(t)$, growing without bound. The string breaks: the budget shifts into the spatial sector identically on each rocket, so no differential ageing; the paradox lives in the spatial-sector geometry, the string breaking as co-moving distance grows as $1/v_{x_4}$.
