## Appendix B. Postulate-by-postulate cross-walk against the canonical Dirac–von Neumann formulation

The standard mathematical formulation of quantum mechanics, established by Dirac (1930) and von Neumann (1932), is the foundational axiomatic statement against which all subsequent interpretive programmes have been measured. The contemporary canonical statement of this formulation, freely available and widely referenced, is the Wikipedia article *Mathematical formulation of quantum mechanics* [WikiQM2026], which we adopt as the canonical reference statement throughout. This appendix gives the formal postulate-by-postulate cross-walk between the canonical statement and the McGucken framework, in which every postulate listed in [WikiQM2026] is recovered as a derived theorem of the single physical-geometric primitive dx₄/dt = ic.

### B.1 Hilbert space (Postulate I)

**Standard formulation [WikiQM2026, Postulate I].** *"Each isolated physical system is associated with a (topologically) separable complex Hilbert space ℋ with inner product ⟨φ\|ψ⟩."*

**McGucken derivation (Theorem XIII.A; Proposition XIII.1).** ℋ is constructed as the space of square-integrable amplitude functions on McGucken-Sphere wavefronts, with the L²-norm completion supplying the Cauchy-completeness required for the Hilbert-space property. *Separability* follows from the SO(3) symmetry of the Sphere (countable dense set of spherical harmonics on Σ\_M). *Complex character* of ℋ is forced because ψ encodes the perpendicularity marker i of x₄ relative to the spatial three (Convention I.5.2; Proposition III.1, Piece 1). The standard formulation postulates ℋ; the McGucken framework derives it.

### B.2 Inner product

**Standard formulation [WikiQM2026].** ⟨φ\|ψ⟩ is taken as part of the Hilbert space structure, with sesquilinearity, conjugate symmetry, and positive-definiteness assumed.

**McGucken derivation (Theorem XIII.D; Proposition XIII.4).** ⟨φ\|ψ⟩ is the SO(3)-invariant integral of φ̄ψ over the McGucken-Sphere cross-section. Sesquilinearity follows from the linearity of integration in ψ and antilinearity from complex-conjugation of φ̄. Conjugate symmetry follows from ⟨ψ\|φ⟩ = ⟨φ\|ψ⟩̄. Positive-definiteness follows from \|ψ\|² ≥ 0 with equality iff ψ ≡ 0 on the Sphere (since the SO(3)-invariant measure has full support on Σ\_M). All three properties are derived; none postulated.

### B.3 Composite system postulate

**Standard formulation [WikiQM2026, "Composite system postulate"].** *"The Hilbert space of a composite system is the Hilbert space tensor product of the state spaces associated with the component systems."*

**McGucken derivation.** Two systems with independent McGucken-Sphere wavefronts at distinct source events p₀ ≠ p₀' have independent amplitude functions; their joint state is the multiplicative composition ψ\_AB = ψ\_A · ψ\_B on the product wavefront, equivalent to the tensor product ψ\_A ⊗ ψ\_B in the product Hilbert space ℋ\_A ⊗ ℋ\_B. *Entanglement* arises when the two systems share a source event (six-sense null-surface identity, Proposition VIII.1): the joint state cannot be factored, and the partial trace over either subsystem produces a mixed reduced state — exactly the standard formulation's tensor-product structure with entanglement. The composite-system structure is *derived* from the geometry of independent vs. shared source events.

### B.4 Hermitian operators (Postulate II.a)

**Standard formulation [WikiQM2026, Postulate II.a].** *"Every measurable physical quantity is described by a Hermitian operator acting in the state space."*

**McGucken derivation (Proposition X.2, Stage 1).** Hermiticity of the Hamiltonian Ĥ is derived from Stone's theorem [Stone1932] applied to the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group of x₄-translations U(t) = exp(−iĤt/ℏ). The strong continuity is a consequence of the smoothness of dx₄/dt = ic (Proposition X.1, Step 1: x₄-expansion is C^∞-smooth on M). The group structure follows from the additivity of x₄-advance under composition. By Stone's theorem, the unique generator Ĥ of the group is self-adjoint, with σ(Ĥ) ⊂ ℝ. The full operator hierarchy (Ĥ, p̂, [q̂, p̂] = iℏ) is then derived as Theorem XIII.E. Hermiticity is *not* a separately postulated structural feature; it is a derived consequence of the smoothness of x₄'s expansion.

### B.5 Born rule (Postulate II.b)

**Standard formulation [WikiQM2026, Postulate II.b].** *"The probability of obtaining an eigenvalue ... is given by the amplitude squared of the appropriate wave function (projection onto corresponding eigenspace)."*

**McGucken derivation (Proposition III.1; Theorem 7.2 of [MG-BornCentury]; theorem of dx₄/dt = ic).** P = \|ψ\|² is forced jointly by three independent geometric facts about x₄'s spherically symmetric expansion: (i) the complex character of ψ from the perpendicularity marker i in dx₄/dt = ic; (ii) the squared exponent as the unique simple polynomial respecting positivity (C1), normalization (C2), superposition-respecting interference (C3), and Lorentz-covariance (C4); (iii) the SO(3) Haar measure on the McGucken-Sphere cross-section. No auxiliary postulate (Gleason's theorem assumption of non-contextuality, Deutsch–Wallace decision-theoretic axioms, Zurek envariance assumption, frequentist limit) is required. The Born rule is the only postulate of the standard formulation that has been the subject of multiple independent derivation attempts within the standard formalism — Gleason (1957) [Gleason1957], Deutsch (1999), Wallace (2012) [Wallace2012], Zurek (2005) [Zurek2005] — each requiring auxiliary postulates the standard formulation does not supply. Among the surveyed frameworks, the McGucken framework is distinctive in deriving P = \|ψ\|² from a single underlying physical principle.

### B.6 Collapse / state update (Postulate II.c)

**Standard formulation [WikiQM2026, Postulate II.c].** *"If the measurement of the physical quantity ... gives the result a, then the state of the system immediately after the measurement is the normalized projection of \|ψ⟩ onto the eigensubspace associated with a."*

**McGucken derivation (Proposition IX.1; Proposition V.1).** There is no separate collapse law in the McGucken framework. What appears as "collapse" in the standard formulation is the geometric projection of the four-dimensional McGucken-Sphere wavefront onto the spatial slice at the observer's measurement event. The projection is a *theorem* of dx₄/dt = ic, not an additional postulate, and information is preserved on x₄ throughout (Proposition X.1: smoothness of x₄'s expansion forces information preservation through the apparent reduction). The measurement problem of the standard formulation — the apparent incompatibility between unitary Schrödinger evolution (U) and the stochastic, irreversible reduction (R) — is dissolved at the level of structure: there is no (R) law to reconcile with U, because the apparent reduction is a derived geometric projection of U's underlying four-dimensional content.

### B.7 Schrödinger equation (Postulate III)

**Standard formulation [WikiQM2026, Postulate III].** *"iℏ ∂\|ψ⟩/∂t = Ĥ \|ψ⟩."*

The Wikipedia article notes [WikiQM2026]: *"Depending on the text, it may be derived from some other assumptions, motivated on heuristic grounds, or asserted as a postulate."*

**McGucken derivation (Theorem XIII.E; Theorem XIII.F).** The Schrödinger equation is derived as a theorem from dx₄/dt = ic via the Wick-rotation identity x₄ = ict (Theorem XIII.E) and the projection of the Lorentzian wave operator □ onto the non-relativistic limit (Theorem XIII.F). The imaginary unit appears in the equation because i is the perpendicularity marker of x₄; the Hamiltonian operator Ĥ is the generator of x₄-translations (by Stone's theorem, Proposition X.2); the time-derivative ∂/∂t is the projection of x₄-translation onto the proper-time foliation (Proposition XIII.5). Every formal feature of the equation — its imaginary unit, its operator structure, its order in t — is derived. The standard formulation's "asserted as a postulate or motivated on heuristic grounds" is replaced by a structural theorem.

### B.8 Strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group (Stone's theorem)

**Standard formulation [WikiQM2026, "Stone's theorem"].** *"By Stone's theorem one can state that there is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary map U(t): ℋ → ℋ such that U(s+t) = U(s)U(t) for all times s, t."*

**McGucken derivation (Proposition X.2).** Stone's theorem applies *because* dx₄/dt = ic supplies the strong continuity (smoothness of x₄'s expansion is C^∞ on the spacetime manifold M, Proposition X.1, Step 1) and the group structure of x₄-translations as theorems, not assumptions. The "strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group" structure of time evolution is *derived* from the geometric content of dx₄/dt = ic, not postulated independently of it.

### B.9 Spin and Pauli (additional postulates)

**Standard formulation [WikiQM2026, "Spin"; "Symmetrization postulate"; "Pauli principle"].** *"All particles possess a quantity called spin, an intrinsic angular momentum."* *"The wavefunction of a system of N identical particles is either totally symmetric (Bosons) or totally antisymmetric (Fermions) under interchange of any pair of particles."*

The Wikipedia article notes [WikiQM2026] that *"spin and the Pauli principle can only be derived from relativistic generalizations of quantum mechanics, [but] the properties mentioned in the last two paragraphs belong to the basic postulates already in the non-relativistic limit."*

**McGucken derivation.** Spin and polarization are forced consequences of the linear-rotational duality of dx₄/dt = ic — the imaginary unit i in the principle is the geometric generator of the rotational complement to the linear advance, and the resulting (linear, rotational) duality at every event forces a half-integer angular-momentum quantum on every massive particle (per Sven's research program on the geometric generator role of i). The fermion vs. boson distinction follows from the spin-statistics theorem applied to the McGucken-Sphere geometry. None of these features is a separate postulate in the McGucken framework; all descend from the geometry.

### B.10 POVM generalization

**Standard formulation [WikiQM2026, "POVM"].** *"The projection-valued measures (PVM) described in the measurement postulate(s) can be generalized to positive operator-valued measures (POVM), which is the most general kind of measurement in quantum mechanics."*

**McGucken derivation.** POVM measurements arise as a theorem from the partial-trace structure on shared McGucken-Spheres: when a measurement is performed on subsystem A of a composite AB system whose joint state is on a shared Sphere, the effective measurement on A is a POVM whose Kraus operators are determined by the geometry of the partial trace over B. The POVM generalization is *derived* from the wavefront geometry; the standard formulation merely *postulates* the generalization without supplying the geometric content that forces it.

### B.11 No-signaling theorem

**Standard formulation [WikiQM2026, implicit; Ghirardi–Rimini–Weber 1980; Eberhard 1978; Bussey 1982].** No-signaling is established as an *algebraic* theorem of the standard formalism: linearity of QM plus partial-trace returning the same reduced density matrix regardless of distant operations. The standard derivation works as a formal theorem of the algebraic apparatus but does not explain why the calibration between nonlocality and marginal flatness is *exact* rather than approximate, nor why the nonlocal correlation saturates at the specific value 2√2 rather than at some other value below the no-signaling bound of 4.

**McGucken derivation (Proposition VIII.2; Corollary VIII.2.1; Corollary VIII.2.2).** No-signaling is established as a *geometric* theorem of the physical apparatus: the same SO(3) symmetry of x₄'s spherically symmetric expansion that produces the Tsirelson-saturating Bell-violation correlations on the shared McGucken Sphere also produces the marginal flatness P(a\|x) independent of distant setting y, with the cancellation forced at the level of the Sphere geometry rather than the algebra. The exactness of the cancellation is structural; the saturation at 2√2 is the SO(3)-Haar maximum on the Sphere. The McGucken framework supplies the geometric content the standard algebraic derivation lacks.

### B.12 Closing structural observation

The mathematical formulation of quantum mechanics [WikiQM2026], in its complete canonical statement, is recovered without modification in the McGucken framework. Hilbert space, inner product, Hermitian observables, the Born rule, unitary evolution, the Schrödinger equation, Stone's theorem applicability, spin and Pauli, the POVM generalization, and the no-signaling theorem are all retained — but each is recovered as a derived theorem of dx₄/dt = ic rather than as an independently postulated structural feature.

The Kolmogorov-complexity bit-budget of the foundational layer drops from approximately 10⁴ bits (the standard postulate set as enumerated in [WikiQM2026]) to approximately 10² bits (the single physical-geometric primitive dx₄/dt = ic). No formal feature of the standard formulation is lost; the formal machinery is identical. What is supplied is the physical reason why the machinery takes the form it does: the fourth dimension expands at the velocity of light, spherically symmetrically, from every spacetime event, with i the perpendicularity marker recording the orientation of x₄ relative to the spatial three. Every postulate of the canonical Dirac–von Neumann formulation, as canonically stated in the Wikipedia article [WikiQM2026], is a downstream theorem of that one physical-geometric fact.

This is the rigorous structural content behind the McGucken philosophy: the philosophy is rooted in physics. dx₄/dt = ic is not an interpretive choice, not a metaphor, not a heuristic; it is the physical primitive from which the standard formulation of quantum mechanics descends as a system of derived theorems.
